In ACC After Dark action, Stanford hosts NC State at Stanford Stadium in Stanford, Calif., on Friday at 10:30 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Wolfpack are 6.5-point road favorites tonight, and my NC State vs. Stanford prediction and college football picks expect CJ Bailey to pick apart one of the Power Four's worst defenses. TOP PICK Who will win NC State vs Stanford: NC State -6.5 Stanford has been completely uncompetitive in four of its last five FBS games and is 1-5 ATS since the start of September. While NC State isn't a powerhouse, the Wolfpack have enough offense to cover up to -8.5 on the road . The Cardinal have lost four of their last five FBS games by at least 28 points and scored seven or fewer in all four (they were outscored 115-10 in their last two FBS games) . With a defense that's ranked 127th in success rate (50.1%) , Stanford's offense won't be able to keep up with the Wolfpack. NC State has scored 31+ points in three of its last four FBS games, all against defenses ranked higher by SP+ than Stanford's (111th). Plus, the Wolfpack are coming off a bye week and should be well rested for the West Coast trip. NC State vs Stanford Over/Under pick: Over 55.5 NC State and Stanford have struggling defenses, which have helped them consistently hit the Over this season. The Wolfpack and Cardinal are a combined 9-4 to the Over, and I like it to hit at 55.5 or better . Stanford's defense has the lowest havoc rate in the ACC (11.3%) and is allowing the second-most yards per game in the Power Four (452) . NC State's defense isn't all that much better, though, ranking 124th in net EPA per play and 133rd in EPA per pass. These two defenses bend and break, ranking the worst in the conference in points per opportunity on defense, though Stanford (5.06) is significantly worse than NC State (3.94). NC State vs Stanford combo Stanford is one of the worst teams in college football, and it doesn't look like Andrew Luck and Tavita Pritchard will be turning things around anytime soon. Though Davis Warren has been efficient at QB, the Cardinal have a dreadful defense that ranks outside the top 115 in EPA per pass, EPA per rush, and available yards percentage (57.3%). Even against an NC State defense giving up 27.7 points per game, Stanford won't be able to keep this close at home against David Doeren's team. The Wolfpack's passing game will be too much, and I have NC State winning 33-24 . NC State -6.5 NC State first half -3.5 NC State vs Stanford prop: NC State team total Over 31.5 After a shaky start to the year, CJ Bailey has been far more impressive in his last few starts. He's put up a 72+ QBR in four of the Wolfpack's last five games and should continue to play well enough for NC State to hit its team total Over at 32.5 or better . In his last three outings, he's finished with an adjusted completion percentage of 77.1% or higher while accounting for just two turnover-worthy plays. His efficiency has helped the Wolfpack climb to 37th nationally in pass success rate (47.6%) , which doesn't bode well for Stanford. The Cardinal allow the eighth-most passing yards per game in the Power Four (255.4) and are the only P4 program with fewer than five sacks and fewer than five interceptions. Stanford is trying to fight the good fight in a rebuild under new head coach Tavita Pritchard, but at 3-4 with only one home game left, it's in big trouble if it loses. NC State vs Stanford: Quick Hits Why does Stanford need this? Three straight road games follow this, but that includes a trip up the road to Cal. The lack of a pass rush and few defensive stops are the real issues, but you can't win if you don't score, and Stanford can't put the biscuit in the basket. Not to get all basic here, but the Cardinal have scored seven points or fewer in the four losses, and 34 or more in the three wins. The ground game has been non-existent against everyone but Elon and Hawaii. NC State is fantastic at keeping the chains moving. Stanford doesn't get to the quarterback and will struggle to hit Wolfpack star CJ Bailey enough to get off the field. Why Stanford Will Win Okay, context time. Yeah, Stanford's offense was putrid in the four losses. One of those came against a nasty Duke defense Durham, and the other three losses were to Miami, Notre Dame, and a Wake Forest team whose only loss is to the Hurricanes. This is one of those focus-test moments for the ACC team from the Eastern Time Zone. This will end around 2 am NC State time, and while these are college kids who can certainly stay awake, the rhythm will be thrown off. NC State vs Stanford Prediction, Betting Lines Don't just blow this off as a layup win for NC State before getting back on the plane to go deal with bigger and better things. The Wolfpack have had to deal with a whole ton of adversity this season, and they keep coming back, but it's 0-2 on the road, and Stanford is 3-1 at home, with that one loss coming to Miami. NC State doesn't have the pass rush to overwhelm the Cardinal backfield, but it'll be just okay enough to get out with a tough late-night win. away.headline: NC State availability report: RB Duke Scott listed out ahead of road trip to Stanford
away.blurb: Doeren initially dubbed senior offensive guard Kamen Smith , junior running back Duke Scott , junior wideout JoJo Trader and sophomore safety Tristan Teasdell as “day-to-day” earlier this week, but Scott and Teasdell were listed as out this week. Smith and Trader, meanwhile, are both questionable. Both Scott, who has rushed for 358 yards and four scores so far this season, and Teasdell missed the Wolfpack’s loss to Wake Forest two weeks ago with injuries sustained the week prior in the win over Louisville. Smith and Trader, meanwhile, also missed the loss to the Demon Deacons after being listed as “game-time decisions” ahead of the home tilt before the bye week. Additionally, the Wolfpack will be without a pair of freshmen for the first time this fall as running back Dylan McCoy and tight end Stephen Brown were new additions to the report, both being listed as out. Coming off the team’s second and final open date of the season, NC State coach Dave Doeren hoped his team was able to get his roster back to as close to full strength as possible. After all, the Wolfpack is set to embark on a six-game sprint to close the regular season. “Your bye week goals change from year to year,” Doeren said Monday evening. “For us, it was getting healthy — as healthy as we could.” Although that was the goal, NC State still has several key players that it will be without when it travels to Stanford for a Friday night clash (10:30 p.m. ET, ESPN). away.blurb: Yousef Mugharbil joined the out-for-season list after the injury he suffered against Louisville, which is a bummer for a guy who has already been through a lot to get back to a point where he’s making an impact on the field. Jimarion McCrimon isn’t listed at all on the report this week, so that’s a positive development, but Kamen Smith is questionable again. Working with a patchwork line is a little easier against the likes of Stanford than Wake or Louisville, at least. Has NC State’s injury situation improved after a week off? No, not really. In addition to missing at least two starting linemen, State will again be without running back Duke Scott, so that’s unfortunate. Not as unfortunate as the Pack’s dilapidated ground game, but not far off. Stanford’s most notable injured player is linebacker Matt Rose, who was a second-team All-ACC player in 2025 after racking up 106 tackles. He hasn’t played in a game for the Cardinal since the last week of September.

away.headline: Stanford Injury Report Ahead of Season-Defining Matchup With NC State
away.blurb: But the program needs to get by without some key players. Ahead of the matchup, the ACC released official injury reports for this week. Stanford has multiple players still listed out, including linebacker Matt Rose and defensive back Brandon Nicholson. He has played at an elite level when healthy, but it is still to be disclosed how long he will be out. Stanford needs him back desperately to improve linebacker depth and production. Rose is the leader of the defense, and his presence elevates everyone around him. He's set to miss a significant amount of time, and it is highly possible that he will not return this season, putting the program in a tough spot. After Collin Wright missed time with an injury of his own last season, Nicholson shined and proved himself as a key player for the defense. Defensive backs Lonnie McAllister III and Chris Garland are questionable, while Lasiah Jackson is probable. NC State will be down some key stars as well. Running back Jayden Scott, defensive back Tristan Teasdell and tight end Vander Ploog headline the list of injured NC State players. Scott, NC State's leading rusher, has 62 carries for 358 yards and four touchdowns this season. With him out, it will be interesting to see how the Wolfpack's offense attacks. Wide receiver Jojo Trader and offensive tackle Kamen Smith are listed as questionable for the Wolfpack. If they return, they will provide a big boost. This game is big for both teams. For Stanford, a win puts them back at .500 and digs them out of a massive hole when it comes to returning to a bowl game. They would reach four wins, which is their total from last season, and would have a path to reaching a bowl game. That path evaporates with a loss. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 6 Indiana looks to rebound from a loss to Ohio State, while Michigan begins again at quarterback Getty Images The Tommy Carr era at Michigan will officially get underway this Saturday when the freshman quarterback makes his first career start at home against No. 6 Indiana . Carr led a second-half comeback last week against Penn State after former five-star recruit Bryce Underwood was benched, and Michigan made the decision to fully turn the operation over to Carr against an extremely good Indiana defense. That will present a major challenge for Carr, but it also shows Michigan's faith in him as the best option against the defending champs. Indiana comes into the game trying to shake off the frustration of a loss at home to Ohio State last week, coming a literal foot away from a win had Nick Marsh been able to keep his feet in bounds on a wide-open fourth-down pass from Josh Hoover . The Hoosiers need to refocus after the disappointment of their first loss in two years, as they head into the Big House to face a Michigan team that may not be elite on offense but will still present a stiff test for an Indiana offense that's been out of sync recently. The Hoosiers are 7.5-point road favorites, but the Wolverines suddenly have a bit of life after last week's win, and the excitement for a new quarterback will create a lively atmosphere in Ann Arbor. Where to watch Michigan vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Michigan Stadium -- Ann Arbor, Michigan TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Michigan vs. Indiana: Need to know Tommy Carr's first start: Carr took over for Bryce Underwood at halftime against Penn State and performed solidly, leading three Michigan touchdown drives -- that came off three Penn State turnovers. While he only threw for 47 yards, playing complementary football and cashing in on great defensive plays to turn them into points is a major step forward for this Michigan offense. However, doing that against a bad Penn State team is one thing; now Carr will face an Indiana defense that's among the best in the country. He'll be tasked with not turning the ball over and taking what's in front of him, but Indiana will know that as well, and Michigan might have to let Carr turn it loose a couple of times down the field if they're going to force the Hoosiers off the line of scrimmage. Michigan knows this will be an extremely difficult first start for Carr and will likely try to protect him with quick concepts and a run-heavy approach, but if they want to pull off the upset, Carr is going to have to deliver a couple big plays Indiana's not expecting. Can Indiana establish a rhythm?: A stop-start offense has been a problem all season for Indiana, and while they escaped the first six games without it costing them, it finally caught up in Columbus. Now they face a Michigan defense that is also excellent and will present plenty of challenges, and Josh Hoover will have to prove he can move the ball consistently through the air. Indiana's offense has been predicated much more on the big play than they'd like this season, as Hoover has been able to create explosives in the passing game to Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh. However, consistency has been lacking, and that's kept the Hoosiers from pulling away from opponents as they did a year ago. Against Ohio State, Hoover threw for 296 yards, but completed just 20 of 40 passes to do so. He will need to figure out how to be sharper in the underneath and intermediate passing game if Indiana's going to have a chance of repeating, and that starts this week given the challenge Michigan will present up front. Elite run defenses: The Hoosiers and Wolverines are two of the nation's best defenses against the run, and that presents real problems for offenses that want to lean on their rushing attacks. Indiana struggled to get anything going against Ohio State, even with Turbo Richard back in the lineup, and they'll be up against it again with a Michigan defense that allows a paltry 2.68 yards per carry. One of the six teams better than Michigan against the run is Indiana, allowing just 2.28 yards per carry, which will put even more pressure on Carr to produce through the air in his first start. The team that can establish some kind of ground game will gain an advantage in this one, but there's a real possibility that neither can break through the walls of these defensive fronts. Michigan vs. Indiana prediction, picks We've got two elite run defenses, one inconsistent passing attack and one freshman making his first start. That is a recipe for a low-scoring battle. Michigan has played five games against teams not named UTEP , and all five games have finished with fewer than 40 points. Indiana's last two games have finished in the 30s as well, as they've faced the two best defenses on their schedule thus far, and it's hard to see a game flow here leading to anything approaching a shootout. The fear here is the potential for defensive scores, but even so, give me the under in Ann Arbor for the second straight week. Michigan (4-2, 1-2) will likely need to lean on its mighty defense to hand the Hoosiers their first losing streak in the Curt Cignetti era. Can the Wolverines pull off the upset against IU football? Our five experts make their predictions: Call me crazy. Call it a wild hunch that goes against all the betting experts. But Michigan has a tremendous defense. IU has given up more than 17 points once this year. It's hard to imagine this offense will be the one to break any of those streaks. Getty Images One week after stunning No. 1 Georgia , Auburn will try to duplicate that performance against No. 18 LSU . Auburn will have the Jordan-Hare Stadium crowd on it side, but the team faces an uphill battle in the pursuit of two major upsets. Going into its open date, Auburn was coming off a loss to Tennessee and needed something to build upon. An upset of the No. 1 team in the country on the road will certainly suffice, and now Alex Golesh must find a way to sustain that momentum. If Auburn is going to give itself a shot to slay SEC dragons in consecutive weeks, it will need to put the game on the shoulders of Byrum Brown again. He totaled 265 yards and a pair of touchdowns against the Bulldogs. On the other hand, LSU will have to be wary of entering a hostile environment given its recent history. The team has lost both of its road games this season, and Lane Kiffin's struggles away from home date back to when he first accepted the Ole Miss job. The Baton Rouge-based Tigers just shut out a shorthanded Mississippi State team in Death Valley, and Sam Leavitt played the first clean game of his LSU tenure. He'll need to replicate that performance in Auburn. Before this battle of the Tigers begins, we have everything you need to know about the matchup. Where to watch LSU vs. Auburn live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Jordan-Hare Stadium -- Auburn, Alabama TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) LSU vs. Auburn: Need to know LSU's road woes: LSU is the clear favorite in this game, but it has struggled to win road games lately. The Tigers have dropped eight straight road games, which is the third-longest streak in school history. LSU is 0-2 on the road this fall, and Kiffin hasn't fared well away from home throughout his SEC coaching career. Between stops at Tennessee, Ole Miss and LSU, Kiffin is 14-16. Winning on the road is hard, but LSU can't make it even harder. Run, Bryum, run: If Auburn is going to put its best foot forward this weekend -- and for the rest of the season -- Brown will have to use his legs to create offense. That worked last week in Athens, as Brown toted the rock on 26 attempts, which included five sacks. The catch is that Brown will be exposed to more hits, which increases his risk for injury. Because of that, if Auburn can get its traditional run game rolling, that takes some of the workload off Brown's legs. Auburn trying to go back-to-back: Can Auburn pull off two stunners in a row? The Tigers haven't picked up wins over ranked teams in consecutive weeks since they rattled off three straight against Georgia, Alabama and Missouri in 2013. The trouble is that Auburn hasn't played well at home against ranked opponents of late, which is somewhat surprising given the general mystique around Jordan-Hare Stadium. The team is 1-9 in its last 10 home games against top-25 teams. LSU vs. Auburn prediction, picks What Auburn did last week will be commendable -- and fans will remember it forever -- but it was also extremely improbable. Georgia out-gained Auburn by 74 yards, and the Tigers barely pulled out a win despite a plus-3 turnover margin. LSU's defense is athletic enough to contain Brown, and the offense is capable of putting up big numbers. It's possible the crowd and Auburn defense give Sam Leavitt trouble, but LSU is capable of winning this game by double-digits. The Tigers enter the game at 5-2 overall and 2-2 in SEC play after shutting out Mississippi State 31-0 last weekend. LSU has looked impressive at home, but both of its losses this season have come on the road. Auburn, meanwhile, is coming off a 27-24 win over No. 1 Georgia , giving the Tigers plenty of momentum heading into Saturday's matchup. LSU has the talent to win this game, but playing on the road against an Auburn team coming off a major victory won't be easy. The Tigers will need another strong performance from their defense and consistent production from the offense to leave with a win. Here are three predictions for LSU against Auburn. The Tigers have shown what they can do when both sides of the football are playing well. LSU opened the season with a 51-10 win over Clemson and dominated last week with a 31-0 shutout of Mississippi State. The defense has been particularly impressive, holding Mississippi State scoreless while limiting the Bulldogs' opportunities throughout the game. Auburn will present a tougher challenge, especially after its win over Georgia. Still, LSU has been productive on both sides of the football and should have enough talent to compete with the Tigers. Brown has rushed for a touchdown in 13 of his last 14 games dating back to last season and has rushed for at least 100 yards in consecutive games. That kind of production makes him dangerous, but LSU has the defensive front to limit his impact. The Tigers have recorded 26 sacks this season while allowing fewer than 16 points per game. LSU will need to pressure Brown while limiting his opportunities to escape the pocket. Our college football expert expects a low-scoring Tiger Bowl and breaks down the best betting angles. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Sam Leavitt of LSU and Byrum Brown of Auburn. Auburn may look like an attractive home dog following last week's upset, but our LSU vs. Auburn prediction prioritize the macro-level mismatch. LSU's defense and net EPA profile lead the nation, whereas Auburn's offense is forced to operate through Byrum Brown carrying the load solo. Check out why we're laying the points with LSU and locking in the Under for Saturday's matchup in our latest college football picks for Week 8. Who will win LSU vs Auburn: LSU -7.5 I would play the LSU Tigers to 50%. Last week's win over the No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs absolutely raises the Auburn Tigers ' ceiling, but it took 26 Byrum Brown carries and three Gunner Stockton turnovers to pull it off. Additionally, Auburn is coming off one of its biggest wins in recent memory. I'm not here to tell you that LSU is a better football team than Georgia, but its profile may be more suitable for this matchup. The visitors sit No. 1 nationally in opponent-adjusted net EPA per play at +0.44 , while Auburn is 35th at +0.14. Brown is Auburn's engine on the ground, yet he ranks 100th among qualifying quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's a dangerous imbalance against a defense that can crowd the box and still trust its coverage. Jordan-Hare will have some real juice too, with belief injected into Auburn's season. However, LSU's down-to-down edge should create separation over 60 minutes. TOP PICK LSU vs Auburn Over/Under pick: Under 51.5 The Under is my top pick in this matchup, and I'd play it to 49.5. Brown is producing 0.41 EPA per rush, fourth among qualified runners, and a heavy quarterback-run plan is the best way to keep the game close . That also bleeds clock. LSU's defense has held opponents to 4.35 yards per play and a 39.2% success rate, while Auburn's unit ranks 31st in adjusted EPA allowed and gives up 5.15 yards per snap . LSU's offense is good, but its opponent-adjusted efficiency ranks 25th rather than among the elite. Also, I still have not seen enough from Sam Leavitt to trust him to make game-defining plays. I don't think his head coach has either. LSU can control field position and reach the low 30s. Auburn landing in the teens leaves enough room for Under 51.5. LSU vs Auburn prop: LSU over 3.5 touchdowns LSU has scored 36 offensive touchdowns through seven games, and Auburn's profile points toward repeat scoring opportunities. The home defense allows a 45.2% success rate, sitting 85th nationally, while generating havoc on only 15.8% of snaps . Leavitt owns a 55% passing success rate, giving LSU an efficient way to remain ahead of schedule and avoid settling for long field goals. Trey'Dez Green 's removal from the injury report also gives Kiffin his 6-foot-7 red-zone target back. Auburn can make LSU work through full drives, but it has not consistently produced the negative plays needed to keep those drives out of the end zone. LSU vs Auburn combo The prevailing theme throughout is LSU's defense. It controls the game, wins the game for the Tigers, and keeps it low-scoring throughout. That holds true early on, which is why I added the first-quarter Under to this combo beyond the previously mentioned two plays. I don't expect either team to come out guns blazing through the air due to decision-making concerns tied to the quarterback. That's particularly true early in the game when the emphasis on either to score quickly is minimal. That should keep the clock running most of the first quarter and start off this heavily correlated combo out strong. LSU Tigers Betting Preview LSU enters its Week 8 matchup against Auburn with a ton of momentum after blasting a short-handed Mississippi State team by a score of 31-0. Although quarterback Kamario Taylor was inactive for Mississippi State last weekend, LSU's shutout victory should re-instill some confidence in head coach Lane Kiffin's locker room following a tough road loss to Kentucky in Week 6. LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt is off to a phenomenal start to his first season in Baton Rouge, already throwing for 1,785 yards with an 83.1 QBR — both of which rank 14th in all of college football. While Leavitt's 14 passing touchdowns have been quite impressive as well, the former Sun Devil has thrown a relatively concerning eight interceptions through the Tigers' first seven contests. Many deemed Kiffin's Tigers a definitive National Championship contender heading into the season, but dropping two SEC games before Week 8 could prove to be fatal for LSU. Saturday's game is a clear must-win spot for both teams, but even more so for LSU, which must face the likes of Alabama, Texas and Tennessee following its matchup versus Auburn. The keys to victory for LSU will be for Leavitt to minimize turnovers and to establish the run with sophomore tailback Dilin Jones. Jones is poised for a breakout performance, as I expect Auburn's defensive game plan to largely center around containing the Tigers' elite passing game. Given Auburn's road upset over then-No. 1 Georgia last weekend, Kiffin will undoubtedly be looking to make a statement in Week 8 before facing a gauntlet of a remaining SEC schedule. Auburn Tigers Betting Preview It has been a whirlwind of a campaign for Auburn thus far. In what really marked a new era for this program, first-year head coach Alex Golesh came in to take over the reins as Auburn's head coach following an abysmal three-year stretch under Hugh Freeze, who won just 15-of-34 games over that span. Golesh gained a great reputation as a sharp offensive-minded coach after a very successful stint as head coach at South Florida . Much of that can be attributed to the phenomenal play from dual-threat quarterback Byrum Brown , who followed Golesh to Auburn. The Tigers' first-year head coach has done a stellar job installing an explosive veer-and-shoot offensive scheme, which is a far more modern spread offense that uses extreme receiver splits and a fast tempo to stress defenses both horizontally and vertically. Despite Brown's move to the SEC leading to some subpar play early in the season, the Tigers' QB is finally starting to find his groove in the pocket, currently posting a top-35 QBR of 71.5. The former USF star has made much more of an impact on the ground, already racking up a whopping 460 rushing yards to go with five rushing touchdowns this season. His passing mechanics have improved substantially as well. In Auburn's spectacular upset victory in Athens last weekend, Brown threw for over 150 yards and a touchdown while also racking up 115 yards on the ground. He has now scored a rushing touchdown in five of the team's first six contests. To knock off the Tigers, Golesh's bunch will surely need another huge offensive performance from its superstar dual-threat quarterback. We're in for a spectacular SEC showdown on Saturday afternoon featuring two teams with everything to play for before they enter the heart of a remarkably difficult conference schedule. From a betting perspective, I favor taking a more unique approach to extract value from this game. The spread gives me slight cause for concern because it could be a potential letdown spot for Auburn following its biggest win of the season. For my primary handicap, I feel confident that both Tiger squads will score at least 20 points on Saturday afternoon, which is currently available at -117 at DraftKings . What the LSU coach thinks Can LSU football QB Sam Leavitt keep a clean sheet? When junior starting quarterback Sam Leavitt has avoided turnovers, LSU has easily won this season. Last time out against Mississippi State, Leavitt took care of the football and worked efficiently and smart. It paid off with a 31-0 victory. Auburn has been opportunistic this season when teams have turned the ball over. Georgia fumbled late in the game last weekend, allowing Auburn to go down and kick a game-winning field goal as time expired to pull off the upset in Athens. Kiffin said earlier this week that he and his staff will highlight the importance of ball security. "As you breakdown your losses and close losses, they're usually not as much about how many plays they make," Kiffin said. "It's more the mistakes you make, and the penalties, more false starts and more turnovers than when you play at home." LSU football offensive staff familiar with Auburn QB Byrum Brown When LSU offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr. was South Florida's offensive coordinator under then-head coach Jeff Scott, he helped open up the recruiting process to bring Brown to the Bulls . So Weiss is familiar with Brown's game as LSU gears up for this matchup. "Really hard player to tackle, similar to playing (South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers) that way. They're different styles, but they're really strong through a lot of arm tackles," Kiffin said of Brown. "He seems really smart by the way that he plays." Brown played for Auburn head coach Alex Golesh at South Florida before following him to The Plains out of the transfer portal. LSU offense should get plenty of opportunities It's hard to score if the offense doesn't have the ball or the ability to extend drives with it. Through six games, Auburn ranks 133rd in college football in time of possession. At 26:54, Auburn is dead-last in the SEC in time of possession. But the situation is not quite like that with Ole Miss , which is second-to-last in the league in time of possession because it operates and scores quickly. Auburn scores just 26.8 points per game, which comes in 13th out of 16 teams in the SEC. While Auburn does convert third downs 46% of the time, its offense only converts touchdowns in the red zone at a 65% clip. Defenses have racked up 23 sacks against Auburn and have caused 15 Auburn turnovers to this point. All of that adds up to LSU's offense likely winning the time of possession battle. The onus, then, will be on LSU to cap drives with points. Lane Kiffin vs first-year head coaches this season It's a small sample size, but Kiffin has not found success against teams with first-year head coaches this season. It also happens that the two matchups with coaches in their first year at their programs were LSU's two road games so far this season. Still, LSU lost both of those road games at Ole Miss against Pete Golding and at Kentucky against Will Stein. That same trend is presenting itself Kiffin again, this time it's Golesh at Auburn. Golesh was the coach at South Florida from 2023 to 2025 before taking the Auburn job over the offseason. While at USF, Golesh hosted Saban and Alabama in 2023 and pushed the Crimson Tide to the brink before falling 17-3. So, this game likely won't be easy for LSU. Kiffin will look to buck the trend against Golesh at Auburn this weekend. LSU football vs Auburn prediction If you are a believer in trap games or letdown spots, LSU's road game at Auburn is a hard game to handicap. One could argue this is a trap game for LSU — also factor that this game kicks of at 11 a.m. — while Auburn comes into the showdown off the program's biggest win in some time, knocking off No. 1 Georgia on the road. Only thing that feels certain about this game is that Jordan-Hare will be rocking and odd things take place in that building. Look for an ugly, sloppy, sleepy game. LSU squeaks one out in the end. away.blurb: The secret to LSU's first road win in the Southeastern Conference since 2024 may have just gotten out. Green, a giant 6-foot-7, 240-pound target for Leavitt, had been listed as “out” for LSU's last four games since injuring his knee as he was tackled early in the fourth quarter in the loss at Ole Miss on Sept. 19. Green caught four passes for 60 yards at Ole Miss. The junior from Zachary High has 14 catches for 222 yards and a touchdown in his three games on the season. He is not even listed as “questionable” for this game, which means he is available to play at Auburn. LSU coach Lane Kiffin could keep Green out anyway, though, as he may be out of game shape and would have an open date next Saturday to get even healthier and more prepared as the Tigers do not play again after Auburn until Nov. 7 at home against Alabama. Green has been seen on the sidelines at LSU's last two games without the knee brace he previously wore after the injury. LSU is also expected to have starting edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, who is second in the nation with eight sacks. Umanmielen, a senior transfer from Ole Miss, left LSU's win over Mississippi State last week in the first quarter with what appeared to be a concussion and did not return to the game. Umanmielen leads the Tigers with 11 tackles for -55 yards and is fourth in oveall tackles with 27. The only players listed as out for the Tigers are previously injured linebacker Whit Weeks (leg) and three players out for the season with injuries – defensive back Dashawn Spears, linebacker Charles Ross and wide receiver Phillip Wright III. For Auburn, backup offensive lineman Tai Buster and backup tight end Hunter Herring are both listed as out, while backup defensive tackle Saint Farrior is questionable. Starting linebacker Xavier Atkins is also out as he was dismissed from the team this week. home.headline: Roman Mothershed injury news | Latest on LSU football TE in Auburn matchup
home.blurb: Green did return from injury for the Auburn game Saturday so it's unclear how involved Mothershed might would be in LSU's gameplan. News Sports Things To Do Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals LSU Roman Mothershed injury news | Latest on LSU football TE in Auburn matchup Cory Diaz Lafayette Daily Advertiser Updated Oct. 24, 2026, 12:24 p.m. ET AUBURN, Ala. – It didn't take long for LSU footbal l against Auburn to have a player go down with an injury. Tight end Roman Mothershed took an unnecessary hit from Jaquez Wilkes on the game's opening kickoff inside Jordan-Hare Stadium Saturday, Oct. 24. The Auburn player was flagged for unnecessary roughness and the team was hit with a 15-yard penalty. Mothershed was slow to get up and was helped off the field by teammates before LSU trainers met them on the field. The junior playmaker was guided to the team's medical tent on the sideline for evaluation. If Mothershed can't continue for LSU, it possibly could be harmful for LSU's spread, tempo attack, especially down near the goal line as Mothershed is a big-bodied target for quarterback Sam Leavitt inside the red zone. Mothershed has filled star Trey'Dez Green's role in the offense after he went down with a knee injury during the Ole Miss game last month. He's caught two touchdown passes in the last three weeks for LSU while piling up 77 receiving yards on five catches. home.headline: LSU football injury report puts Auburn's tackles under the gun
home.blurb: LSU will see EDGE Princewill Umanmielen's return to the field this coming Saturday after his name was not on the injury report for the Auburn game. Jacob Strand, who was formerly playing in the interior earlier this season, has gotten significant snaps at left tackle of late. He and Jo Simmons have a massive test this coming week against Umanmielen, who was previously questionable after missing most of the game against Mississippi State with an upper-body injury. We'll see if the Auburn offensive line is ready to protect quarterback Byrum Brown against it. Stanton Ramil graded out as an 80 on the right edge against Georgia in the epic Deep South's Oldest Rivalry upset . The interior held up remarkably well, with Wilson Zierer and Kenneth McManus taking starter snaps. Brown and Jeremiah Cobb showed out against the Dawgs with their best outings of the season. Auburn's run game could have a symbiotic effect with the Jordan-Hare Stadium crowd and keep the pressure on LSU's defense. LSU football injury report puts Auburn's tackles under the gun Skip to main content About Alex Golesh, Joel Gordon, and Tyler Hudanick must now prepare for a physical freak with a 4.7-second 40-yard dash and an elite bend on Blake Baker's defense. The Ole Miss transfer Umanmielen immediately puts one of Golesh's recent big decisions to the test. Alex Golesh understands the challenge LSU is on the edge As Golesh said about LSU, "Those edges are real, like real real." Not only is Umanmielen a handful, but Tennessee transfer Jordan Ross is also elite. Ross had six tackles and a sack against State this past Saturday. Ross has three sacks this year, which ranks third behind defensive tackle Deuce Geralds's five and Umanmielen's eight. The group is even playing without Gabriel Reliford, who tore his ACL in the spring. The roster Lane Kiffin recruited has an embarrassment of riches in Baton Rouge. Auburn's run game has breakout chance against LSU Umanmielen isn't as renowned against the run. With that said, LSU's defense is better overall against the run than the pass. If you're looking for ways to nab an upset on Saturday and prove the Plains is haunted for favored opponents , controlling the clock is one of the most obvious. Brown is the ultimate wild card for Auburn. If he can keep LSU's defense guessing, opening up running lanes in the middle for Auburn when LSU's linebackers drop into coverage, perhaps Cobb, Omar Mabson, and the rest of the running backs could be difference-makers in a pivotal SEC clash.

home.headline: LSU Star Trey'Dez Green Removed From Injury Report, Expected Back Against Auburn
home.blurb: Since Green has been out, they have had to move Roman Mothershed to tight end to account for the loss. He has had a couple of moments, but clearly isn't the play-to-play threat that Green was. The only update outside of Green is that Anderson is questionable. That would be a bummer as the five-star freshman has been a solid rotational piece along the line. LSU has solid depth in the interior to make up for it, at least. Buster was going to be a contributing lineman for them, entering his sophomore year. He has been hurt all season long, but is expected to return at some point. Herring was a solid blocking rotational tight end for Louisiana Monroe over the past couple of years, transferred to Auburn, but has only been able to play in one game. After suffering a knee injury in the Week 3 matchup with the Ole Miss Rebels , Green has missed the last four games. That has been a brutal blow to the red zone offense from the moment he left until now. There isn't much that a team can do to make up for the loss of a 6-foot-7 tight end who moves as well as Green does. Through those two and some change games that he did play in, he had picked up 14 catches for 222 yards and a touchdown. That would put him on pace for 56 catches, 888 yards and four touchdowns over a 12-game regular season. That, at tight end, is fantastic production, and that feels low for what he could accomplish. Sam Leavitt, Lane Kiffin and Charlie Weis Jr. will be ecstatic to have him back. This is perfect timing as they face a tough matchup with a confident Auburn team that just beat the No. 1 team in the nation. Perhaps having their star tight end will help them curb their road woes. It was take away some depth, but wouldn't change much.

away.headline: Kansas State QB Avery Johnson injury leaves playing status uncertain at Colorado
away.blurb: "A lot of it is gonna depend on how fast this recovery process goes," Klein said Monday, Oct. 26. "He's working hard at it and is doing everything that he can. Some of that is gonna be out of his control in this deal, but we're monitoring it obviously very closely , and our doctors and trainers have done a nice job of protecting him and detailing this thing so we do the right and best thing for him." Klein's weekly presser followed his postgame comments saying there "are a few more questions than answers" regarding Johnson's health. He added that a return for Johnson during the 2026 season wasn't off the table. MANHATTAN — Kansas State football coach Collin Klein labeled starting quarterback Avery Johnson as "day-to-day" ahead of the Wildcats' Halloween game at Colorado . Johnson missed his first career game in his three seasons as a starter in last weekend's 28-17 loss at Arizona State. Klein declined to share details of Johnson's injury , hoping to maintain his personal privacy. Klein said the Oct. 31, 1 p.m. CT kick in Boulder, Colorado, is one of the rare instances he's entered the week without knowing who his starting quarterback will be. Fifth-year Jacob Knuth made his first career start against the Sun Devils, completing 26 of 41 passes for 194 yards and a touchdown, while rushing for 19 yards and another score. The Wildcats had no run game to help him, finishing with 84 yards as a team. Quarterback injuries have been a theme for the Wildcats this season, as every backup also has been listed on the injury report at some point. Klein said Knuth tweaked his ankle twice against the Sun Devils. The injury stemmed from the first quarter of the Wildcats' Oct. 17 win over Kansas during a play in which Johnson fell to the turf at the end of a 59-yard run. He was slow to get up and missed one play, but laughed on the sideline and played the remainder of the afternoon without any noticeable issues. Against Arizona State, Johnson was on the sideline, interacting with Knuth and others throughout the game. It remains to be seen what his role will be this week. "He's able to take mental reps, and he was tremendous on the sideline," Klein said. "He was coaching those guys and encouraging them through the course of things. He's able to be mobile; he's able to throw it and run around a little bit. We're just trying to get him well." Wyatt D. away.headline: ‘More questions than answers’: Kansas State QB Avery Johnson’s return remains uncertain
away.blurb: He added that "it's not off the table" that Johnson could return at some point this season . Johnson appeared on the Wildcats' initial availability report on Wednesday, ahead of the Wildcats' Oct. 24 game in Tempe, Arizona. He was downgraded to doubtful Friday, then ruled out in the hours before the game against the Sun Devils . Fifth-year Jacob Knuth started in his place. "We're still trying to handle things," Klein told reporters. "Our medical staff and doctors are doing a great job of working through everything and making sure that we do it right." Saturday marked the first game Johnson has missed in his three seasons as the team's starter. The injury stems from the first quarter of the Wildcats' Oct. 17 win over Kansas when he fell to the turf after a long run. He missed one play before returning the next drive and playing the rest of the game without any noticeable issues. In his absence, Knuth completed 26 of 41 passes for 194 yards and a touchdown, and rushed for 19 yards and a score in his first career start. The Wildcats only rushed for 84 yards as a team. Johnson was on the sideline throughout the Wildcats' loss. When the defense was on the field, Johnson often helped Knuth. Unless he's back behind center, Johnson would likely have a similar role when the Wildcats travel to Colorado for a 1 p.m. CT game at Folsom Field in Boulder. "Again, there's more questions right now than answers," Klein said. "I think there's a lot just up in the air here in this next week or so to kind of see how things progress. "(He handled it) like a great teammate. He cares about winning; he cares about K-State. He and Jacob are dear, dear friends. He would do anything for this place, and to play and compete... it's just who he is." Wyatt D. Wheeler covers Kansas State athletics for the USA TODAY Network and Topeka Capital-Journal. The hope is Johnson is ready to go to help the Wildcats' chance of moving three games ahead of .500.

picks.headline: Three bold predictions for Virginia Tech vs Clemson
picks.blurb: Virginia Tech football has an opportunity to accomplish something it hasn’t done since 2007: defeat Clemson. The Hokies (5-2, 2-2 ACC) travel to Death Valley on Saturday for a 7 p.m. ET matchup against the Tigers (4-2, 2-1 ACC) on ESPN , with bowl eligibility on the line for James Franklin’s squad. Virginia Tech enters the contest following a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech, while Clemson is coming off a 37-0 shutout of Charleston Southern. Despite the Tigers’ recent success, Clemson has struggled offensively throughout much of the season, potentially opening the door for Virginia Tech to snap its seven-game losing streak against the program. With that said, here are three predictions for Virginia Tech’s Saturday night showdown against Clemson. No. 1: Ethan Grunkemeyer throws for 300-plus yards and three touchdowns. Virginia Tech quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer has established himself as one of the ACC’s more productive signal-callers, completing 167 of 229 passes for 1,984 yards, 15 touchdowns and two interceptions through seven games. The Penn State transfer is coming off another solid performance against Georgia Tech, completing 15 of 22 passes for 250 yards and three touchdowns — though 215 of his 250 yards came before halftime. While Clemson’s defense has been respectable against opposing passing attacks, Grunkemeyer has demonstrated an ability to stretch the field with his receiving corps at his best, crossing the 300-yard mark twice. One player who could benefit is wide receiver Que’Sean Brown, who recorded a career-high 182 receiving yards against Georgia Tech last weekend. Clemson defensive coordinator Tom Allen’s familiarity with Franklin’s offensive system could complicate matters, but the Hokies have enough weapons to create explosive plays. I think Grunkemeyer surpasses 300 passing yards for the third time this season, throwing three touchdowns in the process. No. 2: Virginia Tech forces at least two Clemson turnovers. Clemson’s offensive struggles have been well-documented throughout the season, particularly through the air. The Tigers have thrown just two touchdown passes through six games, with freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds experiencing growing pains since assuming the starting role. Against Miami, Reynolds was sacked six times and threw a fourth-quarter interception that was returned for a touchdown. Clemson’s quarterbacks also combined for two interceptions against Charleston Southern last weekend. Virginia Tech’s defensive front has been one of the bright spots for the Hokies, particularly against opposing rushing attacks. The unit enters Saturday allowing just 87.4 rushing yards per game, ranking among the nation’s best. If Virginia Tech can limit Clemson’s ground game and force the Tigers into obvious passing situations, opportunities for takeaways should present themselves. The Hokies haven’t always capitalized on those opportunities this season, but Saturday could provide an opportunity to change that narrative. No. 3: Virginia Tech defeats Clemson for the first time since 2007 Perhaps the boldest prediction of the three is also the most consequential. Virginia Tech hasn’t defeated Clemson since a 41-23 victory in Blacksburg during the 2007 season, with the Tigers winning seven consecutive meetings since then. Dabo Swinney has never lost to the Hokies as Clemson’s head coach, going 6-0 against Virginia Tech — though it’s not the same Tigers that dominated the ACC in the 2010s. Virginia Tech, meanwhile, has demonstrated significant improvement under Franklin, even if close losses against Pitt and California have prevented the Hokies from entering Saturday with a better record. The Hokies’ previous five games have all been decided by 10 points or fewer, and another competitive contest seems likely. With Grunkemeyer leading the offense and Virginia Tech’s defensive front capable of disrupting Clemson’s inconsistent passing attack, the Hokies have an opportunity to escape Death Valley with their sixth victory. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 24, Clemson 21 THOMAS HUGHES: While the betting lines and ESPN's FPI favor Clemson, I'm picking Virginia Tech, largely because of the Tigers' insipid-at-times passing attack. Reynolds has shone at times, most notably against Miami, but the Hurricanes sacked him six times and forced a fourth-quarter pick-six. Virginia Tech's defensive front has been the bright spot of its defense in 2026, and I expect that to hold true Saturday night. I don't think the showdown will be a gimme by any means - each of the Hokies' last five games has been decided by 10 or fewer points - but I believe Virginia Tech has enough to eke out a victory and become bowl-eligible for the first time in two years. Virginia Tech's last victory against Clemson came in 2007, when the Hokies defeated the Tigers 41-23 in Blacksburg. However, Saturday's matchup presents an intriguing opportunity for Virginia Tech, particularly given the contrasting production from the two programs' quarterbacks. Virginia Tech's offense The Hokies' offensive improvement has been one of the defining developments of Franklin's first season, with quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer leading the charge. Through seven games, Grunkemeyer has completed 167 of 229 passes (72.9%) for 1,984 yards, 15 touchdowns and two interceptions, averaging 8.7 yards per attempt. The Penn State transfer has developed a particularly strong connection with Duke transfer Que'Sean Brown, who leads Virginia Tech with 46 receptions for 616 yards and three touchdowns. Brown is coming off his most productive performance of the season, recording six receptions for a career-high 182 yards and a touchdown against Georgia Tech - a 60-yard score on the second play of Virginia Tech's first drive. The Hokies have also received considerable production from sophomore running back Jeffrey Overton Jr., who has recorded 613 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 103 carries, averaging 5.95 yards per attempt. Overton's contributions extend beyond the ground game - he's added 22 receptions for 219 yards and two touchdowns. That versatility could prove important against a Clemson defense featuring several talented playmakers, including defensive end Will Heldt and linebackers Sammy Brown and Jeremiah Alexander. Clemson's offense While Virginia Tech has experienced considerable offensive success, Clemson has struggled to establish consistency, particularly at quarterback. True freshman Tait Reynolds has assumed starting responsibilities following Christopher Vizzina's elbow injury earlier this season. Through six games, Reynolds has thrown for 943 yards, one touchdown and three interceptions. His struggles have been particularly noticeable on deep passes, completing just two of 21 attempts traveling at least 20 yards downfield. Clemson has recorded just two passing touchdowns this season, a significant departure from the offensive production traditionally associated with Dabo Swinney's program. However, the Tigers have found success through sophomore running back Gideon Davidson. Davidson leads Clemson with 430 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 79 carries, averaging 5.4 yards per attempt. His most productive performance came against California, when he rushed for 159 yards and two touchdowns. Wide receiver Bryant Wesco Jr. leads Clemson with 29 receptions for 340 yards, while T.J. Moore has contributed 27 catches for 244 yards and one touchdown. Perhaps Virginia Tech's biggest advantage comes along the defensive line, where senior Aycen Stevens has emerged as one of the ACC's premier pass rushers. Stevens enters Saturday with 10.5 tackles for loss and eight sacks, including 1.5 sacks and 2.5 tackles for loss against Georgia Tech. That could spell trouble for Clemson, which has surrendered 17 sacks through six games. However, the Tigers possess considerable defensive talent of their own. Safety Corey Myrick leads Clemson with 44 tackles, while Sammy Brown has recorded 41. Cornerback Elliot Washington II has also registered three interceptions. Another important factor will be Virginia Tech's ability to finish drives. The Hokies have struggled with turnovers and offensive inconsistency at times, particularly in their losses to Pitt and California. Against a Clemson defense capable of creating negative plays, protecting Grunkemeyer and avoiding costly penalties could determine whether Virginia Tech leaves Death Valley victorious. Virginia Tech has the more productive quarterback and several offensive weapons capable of creating explosive plays. However, Clemson's defensive talent and home-field advantage make this a difficult matchup. If Grunkemeyer protects the football and the Hokies contain Davidson, Virginia Tech has a legitimate opportunity to secure its sixth victory. The sound is concussive. | John Schneider - SB Nation John Schneider Fri, October 23, 2026 at 8:35 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Hokies travel to Clemson this weekend for what could be the most exciting meeting between the two teams since Dabo Swinney became their head coach, and Tech could never manage to close a two-score gap for the game finishes. Taking in Some Highlights from the Week This mid-season week has been relatively quiet for the Hokies and that might have been the best thing for the team. That doesn't mean people aren't noticing players for individual notices. Luke Reynolds keeps attracting big attention for his abilities and accomplishments. Meanwhile Que'Sean Brown is attracting his own level of attention. The Paul Hornung (1960s Green Bay Packers great halfback/returner/everyman) Award notes its player of the week and that's Q. Brown for his breakout performance against Georgia Tech. Brown also attracted PFF's national and ACC team of the week at wide receiver. Take Some Time, Get a Cup of Coffee… It's always interesting to hear Coach Franklin's Monday presser to get a feel for what the team is up to for the game prep week. Away Means White Uniforms It' looks like the Hokies will be in all white uniforms this weekend. No helmet references have been added but in general when it's all-whites. But it's looking like maroon hats for this one. Staff Predictions It's time to put this one on the line. It's a wince inducing prediction for this one. After Game 1, it wasn't expected to be a win. Yes, we all knew at the beginning of the season that Dabo Swinney had some serious personnel issues that he is still not using the portal effectively to fix, but it's Clemson. The rumors are flying and Dabo's seat is pretty hot at the minute. Clemson is one of the programs looking to get out of the ACC to the greener ( as in money and prestige ) pastures in the SEC or B1G. To keep up that sort of attractiveness, the Tigers need to keep winning at a high level, and they just haven't risen to that level in quite a while. We see the odds and the over/under and those numbers are pretty shocking considering the past performances of these teams. The 2.5-point spread favoring the Tigers at home is nearly a pick 'em. You can't argue with Bryan's take. Virginia Tech football vs. Clemson: Preview, betting odds, how to watch | Gobbler Country It's pretty simple, folks. Virginia Tech can, absolutely, win this football game. I think the spread is accurate. I think it will be close. Virginia Tech's defensive weakness (pass defense) matches up with Clemson's offensive weakness (pass offense). Something will have to give. I never feel good about that for the Hokies. We should all be tired of the Hokies being someone's "get-right" game. Clemson has two passing touchdowns in six games. Don't let them get going. I wanna pick the Hokies. I think the offense will have success against a good defense, especially Ethan Grunkemeyer and Luke Reynolds. However, until the Hokies can prove they can win a game like this on the road, I will give the advantage to Clemson in a close one. Clemson 24, Hokies 21 This one got really hard as the Skipper fired to end the Georgia Tech game. Clemson is 2-1 in the conference, and 4-2 overall. Their offense is just not playing well. Dabo has never found a replacement for "Sunshine", and he's starting a Freshman. That doesn't necessarily make things terrible for Swinney's crew, but it does present a major weakness because Tech's defensive line has been doing very well against the run. So, the Hokies need to make the Tigers pass and get heavy pressure on their guy named Reynolds. The trick is though does Brent Pry have the confidence in the struggling secondary to send that much needed extra man against a shaky QB and offensive line? Clemson is always going to put up a stout defense, so the Hokies are going to have to play a tough game, move fast, find gaps and not make mental errors and mistakes ( especially because Clemson is an old ACC team and "home cookin'" is not uncommon ). If the Hokies can overcome their reticence to blitz and can move the ball and score against the Tiger defense, this one might be relatively low scoring, but the Hokies can win. I'm going out on a limb, here, without being a homer. I think the Hokies take this one in a modest scoring smashmouth football game. Just a Reminder of What's Coming

away.blurb: BLACKSBURG — Following a win over Georgia Tech, Virginia Tech football heads out on the road to face Clemson in a pivotal ACC game. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Eleven players are on this week's report for Virginia Tech, the same as Week 6 against Cal and Week 7 against Georgia Tech. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: The Hokies' loss against Pitt came in spite of them racing out to an early 14-0 lead. The Panthers roared back with a 35-10 response, leading by as many as 11 in the final quarter. Though the Hokies mounted a nine-point rally, fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal was ruled no good. Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Georgia Tech: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies? Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Terry, Wright, Austin, Cunningham) Wide Receiver: 3 (Peterkin, Booker, Stuewe) Cornerback: 2 (Williams, Chadwick) Following its first 4-0 start since the 2017 season with wins over VMI , Old Dominion , Maryland , and Boston College , Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2 ACC) lost back-to-back clashes with Pitt and Cal. Both were by one score, marking the first time since September 2024 that the Hokies have lost back-to-back games by seven points or fewer. The following week, Virginia Tech lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley. The Hokies held a 14-13 lead entering the final quarter, allowing the Golden Bears to pull ahead. Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown with 1:15 to go, but Cal's six-play, 75-yard drive — aided by a pair of penalty calls for roughing the passer (Kaleb Spencer) and defensive pass interference (Kenny Woseley Jr.) — enabled it to score the game-winning touchdown with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech marched the ball down to Cal's 7-yard line with three seconds remaining, but quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's last-gasp throw to a contested Luke Reynolds was incomplete. The Hokies bounced back last week, though, with a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech in Lane Stadium. Virginia Tech held a 24-3 lead at intermission and despite being outscored by 11 in the second half, it held firm. Grunkemeyer threw for 215 yards in the first half, though he only logged 35 more passing yards over the final two quarters. This year, Grunkemeyer's completed 72.9% of his passes for 1,984 yards (No. 4 in FBS), 15 touchdowns and two interceptions. There will be four reports in total: today's report, one report on Thursday and Friday, plus a game-day report two hours before Virginia Tech's tussle with Clemson. The Hokies' contest against the Tigers is set for Saturday, Oct. 24, at 7 p.m. ET in Clemso

away.headline: DT Vic Burley added to injury report for Clemson vs Virginia Tech
away.blurb: Burley, a senior, was listed as questionable again after being added Oct. 22. He was not listed on the initial report Oct. 21. Burley has played in four games after missing the first two because of a suspension. He got his first tackle, a sack, in Week 7 vs Georgia Southern. Clemson wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is listed as out. Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said that Sellars has a concussion and is going through concussion protocol. He's made three catches for 8 yards in a backup role. Defensive tackle Devarrick Woods and running back Jarvis Green don't appear on the injury report for Clemson. Swinney has said that he expects both players to return from injury against Virginia Tech. Vizzina was removed from the Tigers' injury report against California on Sept. 25 ahead of kickoff that night and hasn't appeared once since. However, Vizzina hasn't fully recovered, and he was only available for emergencies against Miami and Charleston Southern. The Tigers (4-2, 2-1 ACC) square off with Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2) at home on Oct. 24 (7 p.m., ESPN). Christopher Vizzina injury update Swinney said backup quarterback Christopher Vizzina is having his "best week by far" of the season and that he's 90% healthy. Vizzina has been recovering from a small fracture in his left elbow after originally injuring it against Georgia Southern on Sept. 12. Swinney said after the Charleston Southern game that he wouldn't have had an issue with playing Vizzina against the Buccaneers, but that Vizzina told him he wasn't ready and that Brock Bradley should enter instead. Trent Pearman and Bradley entered, respectively, after Clemson pulled starter Tait Reynolds with the game well in hand. "I asked him. I said, 'Do you want to go in, or do you want to put Brock in?' And he's like, 'Let's put Brock in,'" Swinney said. "So that was really his call. Coach C.V." away.blurb: Virginia Tech Football News: Key injury updates ahead of Clemson showdown, another sell out Skip to main content About One talking point going into the game, and really a talking point each week, is injuries and how they are going to affect depth charts for both teams. On Wednesday, the initial injury report for the game was released, and Virginia Tech cornerback Cam Chadwick was listed as questionable. On Thursday, another name was dropped, and the UConn transfer was off the list, which is a good sign. However, a couple of names still popped up for the Hokies who sound like they'll be game-time decisions at best. Offensive lineman Montavious Cunningham and cornerback Thomas Williams were both listed as questionable. As far as Clemson goes, defensive tackle Vic Burley is listed as questionable. When Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech, you knew that attendance at games was not going to be an issue with the Hokies' fans. Heck, they came out in droves last season, with a dismal season that saw Brent Pry fired after a Week 3 loss at home to Old Dominion. There are still two more home games remaining on the slate for Franklin and his team this season, and it was announced that those two final games will be played in front of a full house. The game on Nov. 14 against Stanford was already sold out, but now Virginia Tech has officially sold out the Commonwealth Clash against Virginia on Nov. 28. To think, Virginia Tech didn't even need to have two-for-one promos to get it sold out in late November. This is expected to be one of the better Commonwealth Clashes in some time. Virginia Tech Football Recruiting Virginia Tech All-Time Football Lists Virginia Tech Basketball Recruiting Virginia Tech Women's Basketball Coming off a 34-24 victory at home over Georgia Tech last Saturday, the Virginia Tech football team will hit the road for the first of two road games sandwiched around their bye week on Oct. 31 in Death Valley in South Carolina against Clemson. The Hokies will be looking to become bowl-eligible with a win after winning five of their first seven games, while the Tigers come in at 4-2 in a battle in primetime on ESPN between a pair of two-loss ACC teams in late October. NEW AVAILABILITY REPORT Cam Chadwick is off the report for the Hokies, while DT Vic Burley has been added for Clemson. pic.twitter.com/yEN9gsML54 Freshman Benjamin Eziuka played nearly 50 snaps against the Yellow Jackets last weekend and will be ready to go this weekend if Cunningham can't go again. It'll be a tough environment for Eziuka to play at Clemson, but Franklin doesn't appear to be nervous about putting him in. "He's dense; he's powerful in the weight room, and he's super trustworthy," Franklin said at his Wednesday media availability . "Obviously, everybody uses that quote: 'Do your job.' He's that guy. home.headline: DT Vic Burley added to injury report for Clemson vs Virginia Tech
home.blurb: Burley, a senior, was listed as questionable again after being added Oct. 22. He was not listed on the initial report Oct. 21. Burley has played in four games after missing the first two because of a suspension. He got his first tackle, a sack, in Week 7 vs Georgia Southern. Clemson wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is listed as out. Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said that Sellars has a concussion and is going through concussion protocol. He's made three catches for 8 yards in a backup role. Defensive tackle Devarrick Woods and running back Jarvis Green don't appear on the injury report for Clemson. Swinney has said that he expects both players to return from injury against Virginia Tech. Vizzina was removed from the Tigers' injury report against California on Sept. 25 ahead of kickoff that night and hasn't appeared once since. However, Vizzina hasn't fully recovered, and he was only available for emergencies against Miami and Charleston Southern. The Tigers (4-2, 2-1 ACC) square off with Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2) at home on Oct. 24 (7 p.m., ESPN). Christopher Vizzina injury update Swinney said backup quarterback Christopher Vizzina is having his "best week by far" of the season and that he's 90% healthy. Vizzina has been recovering from a small fracture in his left elbow after originally injuring it against Georgia Southern on Sept. 12. Swinney said after the Charleston Southern game that he wouldn't have had an issue with playing Vizzina against the Buccaneers, but that Vizzina told him he wasn't ready and that Brock Bradley should enter instead. Trent Pearman and Bradley entered, respectively, after Clemson pulled starter Tait Reynolds with the game well in hand. "I asked him. I said, 'Do you want to go in, or do you want to put Brock in?' And he's like, 'Let's put Brock in,'" Swinney said. "So that was really his call. Coach C.V." LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Texas is looking to end a two-game skid and get its College Football Playoff hopes back on track against an Ole Miss team coming off its best performance of the year so far Getty Images Arch Manning grew up with the unique culture of Ole Miss all around him. His uncle, Eli Manning, had his jersey retired in Oxford, as was his grandfather Archie's No. 18. On Saturday night, Arch faces the Rebels for the first time, possibly at the lowest point of his career. Questions have swirled around Arch during a two-game losing streak that has the Longhorns on the brink of falling completely out of the polls after rising to No. 1 in September with a comeback win against top-ranked Ohio State . He threw two interceptions, including a pick-six, in the loss to Oklahoma , and last week he lost a fumble on a strip sack with two minutes remaining, allowing Florida to hold on for a win, Manning's first home loss as a starter. Afterward, Sarkisian said he would evaluate the offense, including Manning's role in the offense. Now Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) is trying to avoid joining 1965 Texas and 1957 Texas A&M as the only teams to lose three straight games in a season after entering as the AP No. 1 team. The Longhorns will be without the nation's sacks leader, Colin Simmons , who has a high ankle sprain. No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1) has won two straight by a combined 63 points and has rediscovered its groove following a 28-point win against nationally-ranked Missouri last week. Where to watch Ole Miss vs. Texas live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 7:30 p.m. ET Location : Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium -- Austin, Texas TV : ABC | Live stream : Fubo ( try free ) Follow along for LIVE updates, highlights and analysis as Ole Miss takes on Texas. Ole Miss vs. Texas: Need to know Arch Manning's evaluation : Manning is expected to start Saturday, but how short will the leash be? Backup KJ Lacey has gotten more first-team reps over the last two weeks, fueling speculation he could step in against the Rebels. Manning threw only seven interceptions in 13 games last season. He's up to five picks through six starts this season. "He's our starter, but I need to see a better version of Arch Manning like I need to see a better version of a lot of guys on our offensive football team right now, but we need to see a better version of him this week," Sarkisian said. Life without Colin Simmons : Simmons leads the FBS with 10.5 sacks and 16 tackles for loss. He had eight tackles, four TFL and a sack against Florida before he was carted off in the fourth quarter, and reports have him out three to four weeks. That's a problem against Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , who has thrown a touchdown pass in 19 straight games, tied for the second-longest streak in Ole Miss history. His 20 total touchdowns rank second in the SEC, and Ole Miss leads the FBS in red zone touchdown percentage (87.5%). Ole Miss rebuilt itself after Florida : The Rebels left Gainesville in September after a 52-28 loss Golding called an "old-fashioned butt whooping." The Gators ran for 302 yards, and Ole Miss managed one tackle for loss and no sacks. Since a bye week, Ole Miss beat Vanderbilt 52-17 on the road and Missouri 31-3 at home. Kewan Lacy (122 yards) and Makhi Frazier (101) both topped 100 yards against the Tigers. The road remains the question. Ole Miss is 1-10 in its last 11 road games against ranked SEC teams, and Golding's lone road game as head coach against a ranked opponent was the loss at No. 21 Florida. Kewan Lacy comes home : Lacy grew up in Dallas as a Texas fan, and dreamed of playing for the Longhorns, but they never offered the running back a scholarship. "I can't wait to see them," Lacy said this offseason. He has 29 career rushing touchdowns, third in school history and the most in the SEC since 2025, though Golding has managed his workload since he missed the Florida game. His 13-game rushing touchdown streak ended against Missouri, but he still ran for a season-high 122 yards. Ole Miss vs. Texas: prediction, picks Texas is a 2.5-point favorite, and the SportsLine model projects a 29-17 Longhorns win. History backs it. Ole Miss is 1-6 straight up and against the spread as a road underdog against ranked teams since 2020, and Texas has won three straight home games against top-10 opponents. But is this the same Texas team that has been so successful at home? The Longhorns scored 17 points against a Florida defense that ranked last in the SEC, and the Gators sacked Manning five times with 11 tackles for loss. Texas hasn't scored more than 24 points against a power opponent. The offensive line is a mess, ranking 111th in sacks allowed, and the running game is subpar at 101st. The Longhorns are also 1-5 against the spread this season and haven't covered five straight. Ole Miss has the better quarterback and a run game that just went for 257 yards. Without Simmons, Texas loses the one defender built to wreck Chambliss' night. Texas also lacks championship-level coaching. picks.blurb: College GameDay Makes Official Predictions for Ole Miss vs. Texas Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels will travel to Austin, Texas, tonight to take on the No. 19 Texas Longhorns in a ranked conference matchup with major College Football Playoff implications. Ole Miss will be looking for its third straight win following victories against Vanderbilt and No. 22 Missouri. Texas will be looking to bounce back after two consecutive losses against Oklahoma and No. 20 Florida. Texas will be without key players in edge rusher Colin Simmons and running back Hollywood Smothers. The team may also be making a change at quarterback , as backup KJ Lacey Jr. has taken more first-team reps from Arch Manning than normal in practice this week. ESPN's College GameDay was in Salt Lake City, Utah, this morning to preview No. 10 Utah vs. No. 14 Houston, but still found time to have Desmond Howard, Rece Davis, Pat McAfee, Nick Saban, Kirk Herbstreit and guest picker Dalton Kincaid make picks for Ole Miss vs. Texas. Here are the picks: Mississippi Rebels safety Joenel Aguero celebrates with safeties Nick Cull and Sharif Denson after a defensive stop during the second half at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Desmond Howard: Ole Miss Desmond Howard: Ole Miss The Michigan alumni and former Heisman Trophy winner isn't trusting Texas' defense without Colin Simmons. "Defensively, without Colin Simmons, I don't see how they can stop Trinidad Chambliss. I'm going with Ole Miss," Howard said. Nick Saban: Texas Both Texas' and Ole Miss' head coaches spent time on Nick Saban's staff at Alabama. In a game with playoff implications, Saban backed Texas' Steve Sarkisian to have his team bounce back. "Texas, with their back against the wall, they're going to respond the right way. I'm going with Texas," Saban said. Pat McAfee: Ole Miss McAfee compared this game to a coin flip, saying he wants to pick both teams, but is maintaining faith in Ole Miss' star quarterback. "I'm gonna go with Trinidad Chambliss getting a huge win down in Austin," McAfee said. Dalton Kincaid: Ole Miss The former Utah Ute and current Buffalo Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid followed the trend and put his faith in Trinidad Chambliss. "I'm also taking Ole Miss here," Kincaid said. "I think Trinidad Chambliss is one of the, if not the best, quarterbacks in college football, so I believe they go in there and take down Texas." Three of the four pickers selected Ole Miss. The teams will kick off at 6:30 p.m. CT tonight to see if they chose correctly. Pick: Texas -3.5 Archie Manning never played against Texas, but Arch Manning has the chance to lead the Longhorns to their first win against his grandfather and uncle's alma mater since 2012. It's a good time to buy low on a Texas team I would take to cover up to -5.5 at home against Ole Miss . While the Longhorns have lost two straight, they still have the clear defensive advantage, even with Colin Simmons unlikely to play. The Texas defense ranks sixth nationally in available yards percentage (31.2%) and 14th in havoc rate (20%). Check the college football injury report for Simmons' status before kickoff. Meanwhile, the Ole Miss defense struggled in ranked matchups away from home, allowing 90 points across two games. It's a big ask for Trinidad Chambliss to make up for his own defense again against one of the top defenses in the country. Ole Miss vs Texas prop: Texas team total Over 27.5 While Pete Golding is a defensive coach, his team's defense has been sporadic at best this season. Without Simmons, this Texas defense will take a step back, but not a big enough step for Ole Miss to light it up and make up for its own defensive woes. picks.blurb: Expert Picks: Longhorns Wire staff predict Texas vs. Ole Miss Rebels - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers on cusp of 1st title NFL Power Rankings WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Week 8 Waiver Wire Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or Expert Picks: Longhorns Wire staff predict Texas vs. Ole Miss Rebels Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The term "must-win game" is thrown around a lot in sports. A true must-win game is one that staves off elimination. Well, that's essentially what the Longhorns face Saturday night when Texas hosts the Ole Miss Rebels at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium. Just three weeks ago, the Longhorns were the No. 1 team in the nation. Now Texas is fighting for its College Football Playoff life. Steve Sarkisian has gone from the savior of the program to the hottest seat in America. And Arch Manning has gone from superstar to punchline. It has all gone so wrong so quickly. But Mississippi provides an opportunity for the entire Longhorns football program to put the past two weeks behind it and become the contender they're supposed to be ... on paper at least. We discussed after the Ohio State game that this Longhorns team might only play all-out and all-in when pushed the the brink . This is the brink. Tommy Bresee's Prediction Texas is staring down what seems to be a must-win vs. Ole Miss . The offense has given little reason for confidence and the defense, likely without Colin Simmons, has to contain one of the best QBs in the country. For Texas to end their losing streak streak, they'll need their most complete performance of the season. It's difficult for me to see them mustering that, especially against Chambliss, Lacy and the Rebels offensive attack. Final Score: Ole Miss 31, Texas 21 Jamie Gatlin's Prediction The Longhorns enter their matchup with Ole Miss this weekend on a two-game losing streak. Of late they have been plagued by sloppy play and injuries. Life won't get any easier against an Ole Miss team ranked seventh in the nation. The Longhorns have shown they have the talent to be an elite team but are now full of question marks. To beat the Rebels they will need to turn things around quickly but he last two weeks have not inspired alot of confidence. Final Score: Ole Miss 24, Texas 17 Trey Luerssen's Prediction I really don't know what to think of this team anymore. Could Texas rise from the ashes like a pheonix and play like the contender everyone thought the were? Or will the Longhorns lose three straight games and have one of the biggest falls any No. 1 team in the nation has ever had? Will UT figure out enough of its issues to play well and beat a playoff-calibre team in Ole Miss? Or will the entire Steve Sarkisian/Arch Manning era come crashing down on the DKR turf. The smart money is on the later. Texas and Manning has looked completely lost for two weeks. Desperation can be a great motivator.
