picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs Texas Prediction: Win Or That's It - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers on cusp of 1st title NFL Power Rankings WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Week 8 Waiver Wire Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or Ole Miss vs Texas Prediction: Win Or That's It Pete Fiutak Fri, October 23, 2026 at 8:50 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Some of us are old enough to remember when Texas was the No. 1 team in the country a few weeks ago. One odd meltdown of a loss to Oklahoma, and a way-too-tight loss to Florida later – both games were 27-24 – and now there's no more room to make a mistake. Yes, the College Football Playoff can do whatever it wants, but it has yet to take an at-large team with more than two losses that didn't play in a conference championship. 2025 Texas went 9-3 and didn't get in. This year's version realistically has to run the table to get in. Meanwhile, Ole Miss has only lost to Florida, and considering Oklahoma is struggling, and Georgia and Auburn come to Oxford, it's in solid shape if it can win this. Ole Miss vs Texas: Quick Hits Ole Miss closes with four of the last five games at home, with the one road game in the middle of the run at Oklahoma. Texas gets a home game against Mississippi State next, and then closes with three of the last four games on the road. This is only the ninth time these two have played, and it's the first time they've met since Texas joined the SEC. The Rebels won 44-23 in 2013, but Texas won the first meeting 53-14 in 1912 and is 6-2 in the series. How To Watch Ole Miss vs Texas Date: Saturday, October 24, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: ABC Location: DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin, TX – Week 8 Schedule & Predictions – What Will the CFP 12-Seed Bracket Be? – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – CFN Expert Picks: Week 8 Why Ole Miss Will Win Get some early momentum. Texas was actually up 17-7 on Oklahoma, took an early 10-0 lead on Florida, and lost both games. Texas is going to come out hot. It'll try opening it up a bit and get things moving its way. Ole Miss has to get through the early storm, and if it can come out and do what it does – bam, bam, bam … Trinidad Chambliss hits a few quick passes, and the running game has a little success – that would define the narrative. Why Texas Will Win Quit being so freaking afraid. Ole Miss gives up 237 passing yards per game – the defense can be torched. Let Arch Manning throw, make mistakes, and then come back and keep throwing. Crank up the tempo and take the high-octane fight to the Rebels. Chambliss is great, and the rest of the Ole Miss offensive stars are wonderful, but Texas has more talent. It's okay to win this 45-40. It's okay not to play like every moment is overscripted. You have the better team, Texas – go have fun, and see what happens. Ole Miss vs Texas Prediction, Betting Lines Ole Miss will force Texas to stop being so … Texas. Trinidad Chambliss will be wonderful, but make him do everything. The Texas run defense will hold up, there will be a nice mix and balance on offense, and Arch will be just fine. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Thomas Jones Thu, October 22, 2026 at 1:30 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Texas football has dropped two straight games in the same season for the first time since 2021 while tumbling from its spot atop the polls. This video created with the assistance of AI. Things don't get any easier for the No. 19 Longhorns (4-2, 1-2 SEC) Saturday at Royal-Memorial Stadium against visiting Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1). The No. 7 Rebels boast a Heisman Trophy candidate in quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , and they've beaten three ranked teams behind a dynamic offense and a rock-solid defense. Texas has to face three ranked teams in its final six games of the regular season as well as two old rivals in Arkansas and Texas A&M. If the Longhorns want to remain in contention for a spot in the College Football Playoff, they'll have to beat Ole Miss . Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the Ole Miss Rebels. No. 19 Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) vs. No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1) When: 6:30 p.m. Saturday Where: Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin TV/radio: ABC, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: The weather won't be as crisp as last week, but temperatures will still be in the low 80s at kickoff and dip into the 60s by the fourth quarter. Clear skies, full hearts for football fans. MORE: Fans turning on you is one thing, but former Texas players, too? That's a problem | Golden Texas vs Ole Miss football betting info Moneyline: Texas -165 / Ole Miss +135 Spread: Texas is favored by 3 points. Over/under : 53½ Texas history: Ole Miss All-time: Texas leads 6-2 Last meeting: Ole Miss 44, Texas 23 (Sept. 14, 2013) Most memorable meeting: Texas 12, Ole Miss 7 (1962). In a top-5 meeting that capped the 1961 regular season, the Longhorns held on for a hard-fought 12-7 win in the Cotton Bowl. The favored Rebels outgained Texas in yardage, 319-183, but the Longhorns had three interceptions, including three by Jerry Cook. For fifth-year coach Darrell Royal, the victory gave him his first 10-win season at Texas as well as his first bowl triumph. Royal would go on to six more 10-win seasons and seven more bowl wins at Texas before retiring after the 1976 season. MORE: Steve Sarkisian evaluated 'everything' after Texas football loss. Are changes coming? Know the foe: Ole Miss Last week: Beat Missouri, 31-3 Players to watch: QB Trinidad Chambliss , a 6-foot-1, 205-pound senior, won a court battle with the NCAA in the offseason for a sixth year of eligibility. He's beating plenty of defenses, too; he ranks second in the SEC with 279.3 yards passing per game and has accounted for 20 total touchdowns. RB Kewan Lacey , a 5-11, 205-pound junior from the Dallas suburb of Lancaster, earned all-SEC accolades last season but has battled injuries while carrying the ball 62 times for 352 yards and five touchdowns this season. But he looked plenty healthy last week with a season-high 122 yards against Missouri. LB Suntarine Perkins, a 6-2, 220-pound senior, is off to a quiet start with just 20 tackles and 1½ sacks. But he has 21 sacks in his career, and he's the twitchy kind of edge rusher that has given the Texas line fits this season. Central Texas connections: Freshman quarterback Reese Wise hasn't played this season but boasts some pedigree considering he comes from the quarterback factory at Westlake High School.… Former blue-chip receiver recruit Johntay Cook II signed with Texas in 2023 and appeared in 20 games over two seasons for the Longhorns before transferring to Syracuse. Now in his first season at Ole Miss, he has just one catch for -3 yards. When Texas has the ball Could Raleek Brown be the workhorse this week? He looks like the only healthy back since freshman Derrek Cooper missed last week's game with an undisclosed injury and Hollywood Smothers missed practice earlier in the week with a reported arm or shoulder injury. Brown did rip off a 32-yard run against Florida but had just 15 yards on seven other carries. Ole Miss held Missouri to 39 yards on 26 carries behind a dominant effort from DT Will Echoles, and the Texas offensive line has struggled in short-yardage situations against Oklahoma and Florida. Quarterback Arch Manning talks about "letting it rip," but the fourth-year quarterback has struggled this season while averaging only 215.8 yards a game on 63.9% passing. Ole Miss ranks just 11 th in the SEC in pass defense with 233.3 yards allowed per game, and Missouri's Donovan Olugbode exploded for nine catches and 128 yards. High-paid Auburn transfer Cam Coleman (20 catches, 336 yards, 6 TDs) will try and do the same. MORE: Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning fight for blame in Texas football's offensive struggles When Ole Miss has the ball Texas may have to play without All-American edge rusher Colin Simmons , who leads the nation with 10 ½ sacks but will likely miss the game with a reported ankle injury. Tackle Maraad Waston (three sacks) is the only other Longhorn with more than one sack, which is bad news against an Ole Miss offensive line that has allowed an SEC-low five sacks all season. The Rebels only trail Georgia when it comes to yards per carry in the SEC with an impressive 5.15 in league play, but they've also run it just a league-low 190 times in all games. Texas allows a league-low 103.7 yards rushing a game in SEC play, which means Chambliss could air it out more than usual to a receiving corps led by Deuce Alexander (19 catches, 275 yards). Texas running back Hollywood Smothers (2) runs the ball during the game against Florida at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Texas vs Ole Miss key matchup Texas linebacker Rasheem Biles vs. Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss. With Simmons likely out for the game, Rasheem Biles needs to step up as a playmaker after going three straight games without a takeaway or a forced fumble. And he'll have to do it while keeping an eye on the slippery Chambliss, who has rushed for 127 yards this season. Texas vs Ole Miss prediction Thomas Jones: Ole Miss 28, Texas 24. The Longhorns' offense has its best game in league play, but the expected absence of Simmons is too much to overcome against arguably the top quarterback in the nation. Danny Davis: Texas. I feel like this is a version of the Anakin Skywalker meme where Padmé asks "There is no way that the Longhorns' football season essentially ends before Halloween, right?," gets a blank stare from Anakin and then has to desperately state the question again. Texas wins this game for no other reason than it has to. Michael Shapiro: Ole Miss 28, Texas 27 . This is a perfect emotional spot for the Longhorns, who will take the field with plenty of fire with their backs against the wall. I still can't shake the matchup concerns. Ole Miss has perhaps the best quarterback in college football in Trinidad Chambliss. Texas will be without edge rusher Colin Simmons, perhaps college football's best defensive player. Add in the defensive chops of Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding, and a bounce-back for Texas is no guarantee. We previewed Vanderbilt's offense and defense as they are in a massive transition year. We also list our X factors for the game on both sides of the football. After laying out Kentucky 's path to victory in this game, I will now give my final thoughts and prediction. Kentucky is playing a night game in front of a sold out Kroger Field, and this will be true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis' first road SEC night game. The city is buzzing watching year one of Will Stein and the big blue nation will certainly play a factor in this football game. Kentucky's coaching staff is ensuring this team does not overlook the Commodores, as they are reminding them the beatdown they suffered last season in Nashville and the incident of Vanderbilt players disrespecting the UK logo at midfield last time they were in Lexington. There are plenty of impact players for the Wildcats that remember the whooping they took last season, so I do not think Kentucky will sleep walk their way into the bye week. As we stated when we laid out Kentucky's path to victory, this game is a massive advantage for the Wildcats on the line of scrimmage. Kentucky's offensive line has been incredible this season, and I expect them to get a ton of movement in the running game as well as keeping quarterback Kenny Minchey clean in the pocket. On the other side of the football, Kentucky's defensive line should dominate this Vanderbilt offensive line. Jared Curtis will be facing pressure, but the key for the Wildcats is to get him on the ground and not let him extend plays by erasing sack opportunities. Another key area is always the turnover margin, and Kentucky is one of the best teams in the nation at winning the turnover margin consistently. Statistically, Kentucky ranks third in FBS with a +11 turnover margin, trailing only New Mexico and Notre Dame. This is a large advantage in Kentucky's favor, as Curtis is a true freshman and already has multiple interceptions and fumbles on the season. If Kentucky can continue to win the turnover battle as they have all season, this game has blowout potential. Kentucky's offense has yet to put it all together, we saw them at their best on the road at Texas A&M in a dominant third quarter performance. This could be the game where it clicks for four quarters for this offense. Kentucky ranks fourth in the SEC in success rate and explosive play rate combined. Vanderbilt is dead last in the conference in success rate allowed and they rank bottom five in the SEC in explosive play rate allowed. This is a huge opportunity for the Wildcats to put on an offensive showcase against an SEC team to go into the bye week on a high note. This game is monumental for Kentucky, and we have seen SEC teams struggle the game before their bye week this season. Kentucky has to put together a great game to go into a bye week where they could be a top ten team in the country the next time they take the field if they can get this win. The first College Football Playoff rankings will happen over that bye week and if the Wildcats take care of business, they will be on the graphic. A win here could set up a November to remember for the Wildcats where everything is on the table from SEC Championship to College Football Playoff talks. picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey completed 21 of 28 passes for 158 yards and two touchdowns in the Wildcats’ 21-13 win at Oklahoma last week. The 6-foot-2, 211-pound transfer from Notre Dame has been a paragon of efficiency so far as a Wildcat. On the season, Minchey has completed 68.4% of his throws for 1,551 yards with 13 touchdowns vs. one interception . • Vanderbilt true freshman Jared Curtis is a player UK coach Will Stein sought to recruit while serving as Oregon offensive coordinator. “He’s very young,” Stein said of Curtis, “but in terms of the tangibles of the position, being able to throw it, arm talent, running strength, he is a prototype first-round-type talent.” A homegrown, 6-3, 230-pound Nashville product, Curtis is completing 62.7% of his throws for 1,242 yards and six touchdowns. Ball security has been an issue for the freshman QB, who has thrown seven interceptions and lost two fumbles. Advantage : Kentucky Running backs • Kentucky leading rusher CJ Baxter (484 yards, 5.6 yards a carry, eight touchdowns) sat out last week’s victory at Oklahoma with an undisclosed injury. In Baxter’s absence, third-year player Jason Patterson led UK with 38 yards on 12 carries vs. the Sooners. Former Oklahoma back Jovantae Barnes carried five times for 16 yards last week vs. his former team. • Vanderbilt coach Clark Lea deploys a two-man running back rotation. Senior Sedrick Alexander has run for 270 yards and five touchdowns and is averaging 4.4 yards a rush. The 5-9, 207-pound product of Austin, Texas, has also caught 11 passes for 94 yards and a score. Senior Makhilyn Young has rushed for 232 yards and two TDs and is averaging 4.2 yards a carry. A 5-10, 210-pound product of Midland, Texas, Young has caught 10 passes for 76 yards. Wide receivers • Kentucky’s Kenny Darby was named a Midseason Freshman All-American by On3 Sports this week. The 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, leads UK with 34 catches and 436 receiving yards and is tied for the team lead with three touchdown receptions. Senior Nic Anderson made an acrobatic, juggling catch against Oklahoma — the team for whom he played as a freshman. Over the past three games, the 6-4, 205-pound Atlanta product has caught 13 passes. On the season, Anderson has 17 catches for 197 yards and a TD. • Vanderbilt senior Junior Sherrill is fourth in the SEC in receptions with 41. A 5-11, 200-pound Nashville product, Sherrill has 628 receiving yards and has caught four touchdown passes. In Vandy’s 45-17 strafing of UK last season, Sherrill caught eight passes for 115 yards and a TD. Advantage : Even • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez is putting together an All-SEC-caliber season. The 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School caught five passes for 38 yards and two touchdowns in last week’s win at Oklahoma. On the season, Rodriguez has 33 catches for 257 yards and three TDs. • A transfer from East Carolina who began his college career at Ole Miss, Vanderbilt’s Jayvontay Conner has 13 catches for 146 yards. Cole Spence has six receptions for 72 yards. In last season’s blowout of UK, Spence caught three passes for 48 yards. Offensive line • Kentucky left offensive tackle Lance Heard was named a First Team Mid-Season All-American this week by On3 Sports. A 6-6, 325-pound product of Bonita, Louisiana, Heard was recently ranked the 29th-best prospect for the 2027 NFL draft by CBSSports.com. • Vanderbilt “quick guard” Cade McConnell is the only returning starter along the offensive front from last season’s 10-3 team. A 6-5, 323-pound product of Choctaw, Oklahoma, McConnell began his college career at Minnesota. Center Lyndon Cooper logged 25 career starts at Pittsburgh and was considered a portal-recruiting coup for Vandy. Advantage: Kentucky Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace and tackle Tavion Gadson were disruptive forces for UK late in the win at Oklahoma. Humphrey-Grace, a 6-4, 271-pound senior from Cincinnati, was credited with 1.5 sacks and three quarterback hurries vs. the Sooners. It was Humphrey-Grace deflecting the ball off the throwing hand of Oklahoma QB John Mateer that set up the Ty Bryant interception that was the turning point in the game. Gadson, a 6-5, 303-pound junior from Savannah, Georgia, made eight tackles, 1.5 sacks and broke up a pass. “Those guys are really good players,” Will Stein said of Gadson and Humphrey-Grace. • At 6-7, 305 pounds, Vanderbilt tackle Issa Ouattara is an impactful presence in the interior of the Commodores’ defensive front. A product of Cologne, Germany, Ouattara has two sacks and three QB hurries so far in 2026. Edge Miles Capers leads Vandy with six tackles for loss and has two sacks, an interception and the forced fumble that set up Vanderbilt’s game-winning touchdown on the final play of a 35-31 victory over North Carolina State. • Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey made a game-high 15 tackles at Oklahoma. WLB Bo Barnes was not far behind with 10 stops. It has been a season of starts and stops for fifth-year player Alex Afari . The 6-2, 227-pound Cincinnati product is a member of the high school class of 2022 that the NCAA has attempted to exclude from the new 5-for-5 eligibility model. Afari was eligible for UK’s first four games due to a ruling in Jefferson County Circuit Court. However, the NCAA won on appeal at the Kentucky Court of Appeals, making Afari ineligible for the South Carolina and LSU games. A subsequent ruling by the Jefferson County Circuit Court last week restored Afari’s eligibility prior to the Oklahoma contest. The legal back-and-forth “is frustrating for him and for us,” Will Stein said. “We just got to roll with the punches a little bit. It’s out of our control. It’s out of his control at the end of the day, and he’s responded appropriately.” • Vanderbilt WLB Nick Rinaldi is a stat stuffer. A 6-3, 240-pound product of Dover, Massachusetts, Rinaldi has made 42 tackles, 5.5 TFL, 3.5 sacks and has hurried the quarterback four times and broken up passes four times. MLB Bryan Longwell is second on the team with 50 tackles. Longwell had a TFL in Vandy’s rout of UK last season. Advantage : Vanderbilt Defensive backs • Kentucky senior safeties Ty Bryant and Jordan Castell each had two interceptions in the win over Oklahoma. Castell, a 6-2, 211-pound transfer from Florida, foiled a Sooners’ fake field goal with an interception in the end zone and later returned a pick of John Mateer 41 yards for the game’s final touchdown. Bryant, a 6-foot, 196-pound Frederick Douglass High School alumnus, set up Kentucky’s go-ahead TD with a 42-yard interception return, then sealed the Wildcats’ victory with a pick with 21 seconds left in the game. • Vanderbilt strong safety CJ Heard leads the Commodores in tackles with 52. A 5-11, 210-pound Atlanta product who began his college career at Florida Atlantic, Heard also has made four tackles for loss, three sacks, broken up five passes, forced two fumbles and intercepted a pass. Special teams • Kentucky has not had consistently stellar punting in 2026, but Wilson Berry played a big role in the win at Oklahoma. The Australian uncorked a 58-yard, rugby-style kick that backed OU up to its 4-yard line with 2:43 left in the game. On the season, Berry is averaging 44 yards on eight punts and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line twice. Place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 8 of 11 on field goals in 2026 with a long make of 52 yards. • Vanderbilt punter Tyler Ebel is averaging 47 yards a kick and has pinned opponents inside their 20-yard line on 10 of 27 punts. Place-kicker Brock Taylor is 6 of 8 on field-goal attempts with a long make of 47 yards. For his college career, Taylor is 47 of 53 on field-goal tries with a long make of 57 yards. Long-snapper Cole Marszalek and defensive end Tyler Thomas are still listed as questionable. Everything else is the same, including edge rusher Sam Greene and wide receiver Nic Anderson being ruled out. away.blurb: Vanderbilt football heads out of town to Lexington, Kentucky this weekend to take on the No. 12 Kentucky Wildcats for its fifth SEC game. But before the game kicks off this weekend, we have to know who is going to be available Saturday night. Wednesday night, the SEC released its initial player availability reports leading up to this weekend’s slate of games. What was not know were the statuses of EDGE Brian Allen Jr., safety Dontae Carter and offensive lineman Mitchell Smith. On the first injury report, Allen Jr. is officially listed as out while Carter is listed as questionable and Smith is listed as probable. Tuesday, Vanderbilt head coach Clark Lea announced that Allen Jr. did not practice due to an ankle injury, but Carter did practice wearing a no-contact jersey. In the case of Smith, Lea sounded hopeful Tuesday that he would be able to play after missing the last two games. In addition to those three, linebacker Josiah Broxton is doubtful for Saturday's game while safety Davin Chandler is listed as questionable. The Commodores already knew going into the week it was going to be missing backup quarterback Blaze Berlowitz, cornerback Jaylin Lackey, defensive lineman Aaron Bryant and offensive lineman Gunner Givens. In recent weeks, Lea announced season-ending injuries to Givens and Bryant and a collarbone injury to Berlowitz. Vanderbilt will continue to be without linebacker Jamison Curtis, wide receiver Kahden Smith and defensive lineman Nikhil Jefferson Lea will likely give updates on his guys Thursday from tonight's injury report as he usually does. This weekend’s game between Vanderbilt and Kentucky is significant to both teams in different ways. Injuries to Ohio State’s Julian Sayin, Oregon’s Dante Moore, and UCLA’s Nico Iamaleava are among the most notable quarterbacks who have suffered injuries. One of those Big Ten teams fortunate to have the same starting quarterback they began the season with is the No. 16 USC Trojans, led by Jayden Maiava. The Trojans and Maiava will face another road test on Saturday night against the Wisconsin Badgers at Camp Randall Stadium. With Julian Sayin recently injured and the Trojans set to host the No. 3 Ohio State Buckeyes on Halloween night at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, USC has a golden opportunity to make a statement and boost its College Football Playoff chances with wins over the Wisconsin Badgers and the Buckeyes. The Trojans are expected to face former three-star recruit and Mission Viejo, California native, Luke Fahey when they play the Buckeyes on Oct. 31 at the Coliseum. The show referenced quarterback uncertainty throughout the conference, though Davis was quick to point out the continuity that USC has had with quarterback Jayden Maiava. "So let me ask you this. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Wisconsin's Huge Primetime Clash With No. 16 USC
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Wisconsin's Huge Primetime Clash With No. 16 USC Skip to main content SI.COM WISCONSIN ATHLETICS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS FOOTBALL BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS BASKETBALL Saturday night in Camp Randall Stadium could easily set the tone for the rest of the year for Wisconsin football. A win would instantly erase the pain from Week 7 out in Los Angeles, as it would represent Wisconsin's first victory over a legitimately good opponent and give head coach Luke Fickell another top-20 upset on his resume for the 2026 season, which would go a long way in helping him prove he's the man for the job in Madison. A loss, on the other hand, would even up the Badgers' Big Ten record at 2-2 and set them up with a must-win on Halloween in Iowa City, a situation nobody wants to be in. As Wisconsin continues prep for the Trojans , here's three bold predictions for the Saturday night showdown: Wisconsin shuts down star Trojans' tailback King Miller USC Trojans running back King Miller. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect All week long in the lead-up to UCLA, all we heard about was the Bruins' rugged ground game. A supposedly unstoppable force of nature, headlined by star ball-carrier Wayne Knight, was supposed to run rampant over the Badgers' front seven. All week long in the lead-up to UCLA, all we heard about was the Bruins' rugged ground game. A supposedly unstoppable force of nature, headlined by star ball-carrier Wayne Knight, was supposed to run rampant over the Badgers' front seven. Instead, Wisconsin held the Bruins to 44 rushing yards through the first three quarters (120 after a fourth quarter of mostly clock control from UCLA) while Knight himself posted just 23 yards on 13 carries. All told, UCLA averaged just 3.2 yards per carry. Surprisingly, that didn't matter because the Badgers couldn't contain Bruins' quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who completed 67% of his passes while tossing for 264 yards. But Wisconsin made a point; even the best rushing attacks in college football should expect to struggle against the Cardinal and White. USC has two very capable backs in King Miller (114 carries, 595 yards, four touchdowns) and Waymond Jordan (63 carries, 287 yards and two scores). However, the Trojans' ground game as a whole ranks just 77th nationally, one spot above the Badgers — both teams run for 152 yards per game. While USC's backs are capable, this isn't the most impressive rushing attack and Wisconsin just proved that it can make even the best ground games in the country struggle mightily. Miller has yet to run for fewer than 45 yards this season; I foresee that happening Saturday night. Colton Joseph takes care of the ball all night Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After a rough three-interception outing in the upset win over then-No. 13 Penn State, Colton Joseph has taken care of the football, at least through the air. He's lost two fumbles, neither of which were recovered by the defense, but he's also gone two straight games without throwing an interception for the first time in his Badgers career. After a rough three-interception outing in the upset win over then-No. 13 Penn State, Colton Joseph has taken care of the football, at least through the air. He's lost two fumbles, neither of which were recovered by the defense, but he's also gone two straight games without throwing an interception for the first time in his Badgers career. Against USC, there's no reason why he can't make it three. The Trojans have only intercepted three passes this fall across seven games; there's only 11 FBS programs that've played as many games and picked off fewer passes. Their pass defense as a whole has left plenty to be desired; USC is allowing 239 passing yards per game, good for 110th nationally. Joseph has also cut down on the "turnover-worthy plays," according to Pro Football Focus. After he combined for eight over the Badgers' first four games, he has just one over the last two games. The turnover battle is going to be huge in order to pull off an upset like this, but I think Joseph can keep it clean Saturday night. Wisconsin benches PJ Wilkins Wisconsin offensive lineman PJ Wilkins. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Given how he's played, this wouldn't be a bold prediction under normal circumstances. But the Badgers have insisted on trotting him out there with the starters, and that was painfully clear in Pasadena when they moved Stylz Blackmon to center in place of the injured starter Austin Kawecki, despite the fact that Kawecki's backup Ryan Cory played well in his stead, which also forced Wilkins to start at right guard. Given how he's played, this wouldn't be a bold prediction under normal circumstances. But the Badgers have insisted on trotting him out there with the starters, and that was painfully clear in Pasadena when they moved Stylz Blackmon to center in place of the injured starter Austin Kawecki, despite the fact that Kawecki's backup Ryan Cory played well in his stead, which also forced Wilkins to start at right guard. At what point does Wisconsin give up on Wilkins as a starting-caliber offensive lineman this season? It's tried him at three spots — left tackle, right tackle and right guard — all of which have been problematic. He easily "leads" the team with 12 pressures, per Pro Football Focus, although having watched the all-22 tape I'd venture to say that's a generously low estimate. He just doesn't appear to have the quickness to hold up in pass protection. “It’s been a little bit difficult. When guys get dinged up, in particular Kawecki and moving Stylz back in there, we just felt like that was our best five," Fickell said this week . "We gotta find a way to make sure we have our best five up front every week.” Unfortunately, it's pretty clear the Badgers' "best five" doesn't include Wilkins at this point in time. With Kawecki probable as of the Wednesday injury report, he could return to center, meaning Blackmon could return to right guard. picks.headline: Staff Predictions: Can Wisconsin Ride Home Crowd to Win vs. No. 16 USC?
picks.blurb: Staff Predictions: Can Wisconsin Ride Home Crowd to Win vs. No. 16 USC? Skip to main content SI.COM WISCONSIN ATHLETICS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS FOOTBALL BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS BASKETBALL Wisconsin missed out on a big opportunity to knock off its second top-15 team on the road last week, letting a winnable game at then-No. 12 UCLA slip through its fingers. The Badgers have a chance to right the ship and topple a team perched just outside the top-15 with the No. 16 USC Trojans coming to town. This is an absolutely enormous game for both coaches/programs in terms of what the expectations were ahead of each team's season. The noise at both schools would get significantly louder with a loss, their respective coaches' seats would get hotter . Ahead of the primetime showdown with USC, Badgers On SI's staff offers up roundtable predictions for the Week 8 clash: Seamus Rohrer, Editor Wisconsin's defense, which ranks No. 16 nationally allowing just 286.7 yards per game, gives them a chance against most teams. Whether or not that's a legitimate, fighting chance depends on what happens when they're on the sideline and quarterback Colton Joseph and the offense have the ball. I do expect the Badgers to be able to limit the Trojans' ground game. It's going to come down to whether or not Wisconsin can get off the field against one of the best third-down offenses in the country after it allowed a backup quarterback to pass for 150 yards on third down alone in Pasadena. When Joseph and company have the ball, what matters is how much Wisconsin can take advantage of a porous USC secondary, as well as how its struggling offensive front can hold up against some talented front seven players on the Trojans' defense, namely true freshman defensive end Luke Wafle. Ultimately, can the Badgers' offense keep pace with the high-flying Trojans? They haven't given me real reason to believe they can. Prediction: USC 27, Wisconsin 17 Wisconsin Badgers head coach Luke Fickell. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Drew Gentile, Staff Writer Drew Gentile, Staff Writer Last week, I believed in Wisconsin, and like the rest of the fanbase, was disappointed in the result. I'm not under the impression that it was a back-breaking loss, but it certainly diminished my confidence to a certain extent. All that said, UCLA is one of the best defenses in the country, while USC has been shaky on that side of the ball. For that reason, I think the offense bounces back, at least a little bit. My primary concern, however, is Jayden Maiava. Ty Dieffenbach had his way with Wisconsin's soft zone last week, and Maiava is in another stratosphere. Ultimately, I think this is a game the Badgers could win, but until I see a quality effort offensively, including success from Joseph through the air, I'm not betting on Wisconsin to keep up offensively for four quarters. Prediction: USC 24, Wisconsin 16 Jeremy Schneider, Staff Writer The UCLA loss last week stings, but it doesn’t mean Wisconsin can’t win this one. USC has struggled on the road since joining the Big Ten, and its defense is far from a reliable unit. That said, the Trojans can light up the scoreboard behind star quarterback Jayden Maiava. Wisconsin’s defense, particularly against the run, has been solid, but defensive coordinator Mike Tressel’s overreliance on soft zone coverage remains a concern. Ty Dieffenbach picked apart the zone to keep the chains moving last week. If a quarterback making his first FBS start can do that, what might a star like Maiava accomplish? Factor in Javan Robinson’s questionable status, and I’m concerned. Moving the ball should be easier against USC’s defense, but Colton Joseph still has plenty to prove with his arm against a higher-caliber opponent. This is a winnable game for Wisconsin, but I ultimately expect the Trojans to pull away late. Prediction : USC 28, Wisconsin 20 Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph (1) hands off to running back Abu Sama III (3). | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Benjamin Worgull, Staff Writer Benjamin Worgull, Staff Writer There's a lot of truth to the old adage that "offense scores points, but defense wins championships." Wisconsin has a defense that has shown to be title worthy, allowing a Big Ten best 13.3 points per game and 284.0 yards per game during conference play. The problem is that UW's offense hasn't risen to that title level yet. While there was a blip of hope with its 31-point performance against Michigan State, UW slogged its way to a 213-yard evening against the Bruins, complete with a paltry 66 passing yards on six completions from Colton Joseph. Those numbers aren't going to beat anybody, especially a USC team that might be the best collection of individual talent the Badgers will see this season. The Trojans' defense isn't great (350 ypg, 63rd FBS) but they have shown the ability to slow the run (111 ypg, 32nd FBS). A one-dimensional offense rarely yields results, especially when the UW offense has a quarterback that hasn't truly found a groove yet. I feel like we were slightly duped by UW's four-game winning streak, which includes two Big Ten wins over two current winless conference teams. These next two games are huge opportunities for Fickell to show how his program is progressing, although I have a feeling they aren't going to be pretty. Prediction: USC 34, Wisconsin 21 Christian Borman, Staff Writer The Wisconsin offense's struggles last week at UCLA were definitely concerning. Things felt disjointed, and most of the production fell on Colton Joseph to keep things moving. The offensive line is still a work in progress, making problems of it's own. If this offense continues to be a problem and cannot sustain drives, the success of the game will land squarely on the shoulders of the defense. While I think the Badgers have a good defense, even the best defenses will wear down if they are always on the field. With the way the Trojans' offense can put up points, Wisconsin's best chance at winning this game will be taking the air out of the ball and dominating the time of possession. They need to get the running game going, whether it's with the running backs or Colton Joseph, and have long drives that end in points. The less Jayden Maiava is on the field, the better. But after last week at UCLA, there isn't a whole lot of evidence that shows me the Wisconsin offense is capable of doing that. picks.blurb: ESPN predicts the final score of Wisconsin football vs. USC in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers on cusp of 1st title NFL Power Rankings WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Week 8 Waiver Wire Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or ESPN predicts the final score of Wisconsin football vs. USC in Week 8 Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Wisconsin Badgers have a chance to virtually guarantee themselves bowl eligibility this weekend against the No. 15 USC Trojans . With a win, Luke Fickell's side will be pushed to 5-2, with the season's most challenging games largely out of the way. However, standing in the way of a 5-2 record is one of the nation's most prolific offenses who average 462.4 yards per game. The Trojans are 6-1, with one loss coming against the Oregon Ducks in a high-scoring 41-27 affair. ESPN's Bill Connelly's SP+ metric is one of the most widely accepted measures in all of college football, and unfortunately for Wisconsin fans, the Badgers are projected to lose 28-23. What will be the deciding factor? The biggest storyline going into this will be one of the nation's best offenses (USC) vs. one of the best defenses (Wisconsin). While each team will have its fair share of plays to cancel one another out on that side, this will be a game that will be decided by whether Wisconsin's offense can put together its best performance of the season. With the Badgers averaging just 341 yards per game, until they prove otherwise, there is little reason to think this offense will turn things around this weekend. Ryan Minion Sat, October 24, 2026 at 3:03 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Get ready to "Jump Around" as the nation's 16th-ranked USC Trojans head to Madison for a Big Ten clash with the Wisconsin Badgers at their home, Camp Randall Stadium. Let's break down the betting angles for Saturday's contest and bring you a same-game parlay (SGP) you can get behind when wagering on Week 8's action. So, here are my Wisconsin vs. USC picks and college football same-game parlay for Saturday, October 24. USC RB King Miller 60+ Rush Yds Wisconsin Alt. Spread +10.5 Parlay Odds: +104 ( DraftKings ) Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page . Wisconsin vs. USC Odds For the first leg of our same-game parlay for Saturday night's Big Ten showdown, let's target Southern California 's leading rusher, King Miller . Despite Wisconsin boasting an elite defensive unit that has allowed its first six opponents just 16.7 points per game, the Badgers' front seven is not as efficient when it comes to containing opposing rushers. Though the Badgers are typically renowned for their overwhelming size in the trenches, head coach Luke Fickell's bunch has been quite vulnerable when matched up against elite running backs. Miller fits the bill. Wisconsin's defense has allowed opposing rushers over 152 yards per game, which could prove fatal against a player of Miller's caliber. He ranks 23rd in the country with 595 yards on the ground heading into Week 8. Though, on the contrary, the Badgers boast an elite secondary that ranks inside the top 20 in all of college football in both EPA Per Pass allowed (10th) and Passing Success Rate allowed (19th). For a Lincoln Riley offense that relies heavily on the superb play of star quarterback Jayden Maiava , expect the Trojans to slightly change course by giving Miller far more volume out of the backfield. Feel confident backing Miller to record at least 60 rushing yards (-178) in what should provide a solid foundation for our SGP on Saturday night. For the back end of our Saturday SGP, we're backing the Badgers at an extremely steep alternate line of 10.5, which has a -364 price at DraftKings. USC is coming off consecutive victories over Washington and Penn State, both of which went down to the wire. However, the primary concern for Riley's Trojans is that they must play both Ohio State and Indiana in back-to-back contests following their Week 8 clash with Wisconsin. The Badgers are coming off a disappointing defeat to an extremely well-coached UCLA team and now return home with a ton of motivation. Camp Randall Stadium in Madison is a notoriously difficult venue to escape with an outright victory, and while USC has proven it's battle-tested on the road, it would be very surprising if this game doesn't come down to the final few minutes. The Trojans are far more comfortable relying on their explosive offense to win football games, and I don't envision Riley's bunch being able to put up its typical 30-point performances against a Badger defense that ranks 24th in the country in opponent PPG at 16.7. While we're playing it safe by backing the Badgers at an extremely steep alternate number, don't be surprised if Wisconsin wins outright in what should be a very hostile environment in Madison. away.blurb: There's no timetable for Sayin's return. Ohio State coach Ryan Day said on Oct. 20 that the quarterback is out "indefinitely," and the Buckeyes are planning on heading to the College Football Playoff without him. The first Ohio State-USC availability report comes out on Oct. 28. Sayin, who exited the Indiana game with an injury, will not play against USC and is out for "several weeks" according to Day. After a week off, Ohio State football embarks on a difficult stretch, starting with a road trip to face Southern California on Oct. 31. The Buckeyes have a 6-1 record that includes a loss to Texas in Week 2. But during a 19-15 win over defending champion Indiana , Ohio State lost starting quarterback Julian Sayin for an extended period with an unspecified injury. After Sayin left in the fourth quarter of the OSU-Indiana game and went to the locker room, freshman Luke Fahey replaced him. Sayin later reappeared on the sideline in a sling. away.headline: Initial injury report released for Wisconsin football vs. No. 16 USC
away.blurb: Whether he just wasn’t quite ready or the Wisconsin staff wanted to play it safe, he stayed out against the Bruins, with more than half a season left. Stylz Blackmon, who had been playing right guard, moved to center to replace Kawecki, while PJ Wilkins slotted into guard. Now, Kawecki has been upgraded to ‘Probable’ ahead of the Badgers’ matchup with the Trojans. Kawecki’s return would be a nice boost for the offensive line that struggled mightily against UCLA last week. A pair of starters are ‘questionable’ for Saturday Two starters popped up on the report this week that we didn’t expect. Wide receiver Malachi Coleman and cornerback Javan Robinson are both listed as ‘questionable’ for Saturday. RB Nate Palmer remains ‘doubtful’ The Badgers got Abu Sama back off the injury report last week, but injuries remain at the position. After missing last week’s game against UCLA, Nate Palmer remains ‘doubtful’ for this week’s game. Palmer has received only a handful of carries this season, but he has been a constant presence on special teams and the team’s primary kick returner, returning six kicks for an average of 28.2 yards per return. Christian Borman Oct 22, 2026 Share Wisconsin Badgers wide receiver Malachi Coleman. Photo credit: UW Athletics The Wisconsin football team has released its initial availability report ahead of its matchup with USC this Saturday evening. Some players are trending in the right direction after missing time, but a couple of names on the report weren’t expected. Here’s where things stand three days ahead of the matchup with the Trojans. Austin Kawecki is trending in the right direction Starting center Austin Kawecki left in the middle of the Badgers’ game with Michigan State in Week 5. With a bye week to rest, there was hope he would be back for the Badgers’ road game against UCLA in Week 7. Javan Robinson has been the most consistent cornerback for the Badgers this season. If he misses the game, it would be a massive blow to the defense, especially in a week when they face one of the best passing quarterbacks in the country, Jordan Maiava. On top of that, the cornerback depth has already taken a hit this year after Cai Bates was lost for the season with a knee injury early in the year. Losing Coleman wouldn’t be ideal, either. But the passing attack for the Badgers has been inconsistent, and even after his breakout game against Notre Dame in Week 1, he hasn’t been the force we all hoped he’d be. Fortunately for the Badgers, they just got Jaylon Domingeaux back from injury last week and caught a pair of passes, so there is at least some more depth at receiver. away.headline: USC football returned to its troubling old ways - will it ever change?
away.blurb: Here is what we learned about the USC Trojans in Week 8: Physicality remains a huge concern with this team The Trojans got dominated in every facet of the game against the Wisconsin Badgers. The Badgers imposed their will for 4 quarters. Defensively, the Badgers held the Trojans to -17 yards on the ground. While the Badgers ran for 142 yards. Having the #1 recruiting class and a ton of talent does not matter when that is the end result. The theme surrounding the Trojans being a team that can get dominated by more physical teams has been present for years now under Lincoln Riley. This is a notion that poorly reflects the current identity of this team. Something has to change. The road woes are back and unsolved With the win against the Penn State Nittany Lions, I thought the road struggles were a thing of the past. With USC getting played off the field in Week 8, the road woes are a big part of this team's makeup. USC did not show up ready to play at Camp Randall Stadium, and that was evident from the start of the game. Taniela Tupou is a potential legitimate weapon The one good thing about USC's loss is that it gave a great opportunity to evaluate some young talent. Tupou showed he is more than capable of performing in a big game. He was the standout, and following this game, he needs more opportunity. He can become the next key contributing freshman for USC. The loss to Wisconsin will define the season With the upcoming schedule, the Trojans have it clear as day that they could not afford to lose last week's game against the Badgers. Prior to the week, there was a path for the Trojans to finish at the top of the Big Ten; now there is a much more likely path for them to have a disappointing 7-5 finish to the season. There is also a path for Lincoln Riley to be coaching another team next season. When it is time to look back on the season, this will be the game that is the headline and the game that put all excitement for this team to a halt. USC still cannot hang in the Big Ten Every season since the Trojans joined the Big Ten, there is a game or maybe 2 in which the Trojans look worse than their Big Ten opponent. Last season it was a loss to the Illinois Fighting Illini. This season it was Saturday's loss to Wisconsin. In a high-stakes Big Ten game, the trend is that the Trojans will leave that game not looking like a Big Ten team. Getting embarrassed by an inconsistent Wisconsin Badgers team on the road is unacceptable. Lincoln Riley has not proved he can beat Big Ten teams on a consistent basis just yet. home.blurb: Whether he just wasn’t quite ready or the Wisconsin staff wanted to play it safe, he stayed out against the Bruins, with more than half a season left. Stylz Blackmon, who had been playing right guard, moved to center to replace Kawecki, while PJ Wilkins slotted into guard. Now, Kawecki has been upgraded to ‘Probable’ ahead of the Badgers’ matchup with the Trojans. Kawecki’s return would be a nice boost for the offensive line that struggled mightily against UCLA last week. A pair of starters are ‘questionable’ for Saturday Two starters popped up on the report this week that we didn’t expect. Wide receiver Malachi Coleman and cornerback Javan Robinson are both listed as ‘questionable’ for Saturday. RB Nate Palmer remains ‘doubtful’ The Badgers got Abu Sama back off the injury report last week, but injuries remain at the position. After missing last week’s game against UCLA, Nate Palmer remains ‘doubtful’ for this week’s game. Palmer has received only a handful of carries this season, but he has been a constant presence on special teams and the team’s primary kick returner, returning six kicks for an average of 28.2 yards per return. Christian Borman Oct 22, 2026 Share Wisconsin Badgers wide receiver Malachi Coleman. Photo credit: UW Athletics The Wisconsin football team has released its initial availability report ahead of its matchup with USC this Saturday evening. Some players are trending in the right direction after missing time, but a couple of names on the report weren’t expected. Here’s where things stand three days ahead of the matchup with the Trojans. Austin Kawecki is trending in the right direction Starting center Austin Kawecki left in the middle of the Badgers’ game with Michigan State in Week 5. With a bye week to rest, there was hope he would be back for the Badgers’ road game against UCLA in Week 7. Javan Robinson has been the most consistent cornerback for the Badgers this season. If he misses the game, it would be a massive blow to the defense, especially in a week when they face one of the best passing quarterbacks in the country, Jordan Maiava. On top of that, the cornerback depth has already taken a hit this year after Cai Bates was lost for the season with a knee injury early in the year. Losing Coleman wouldn’t be ideal, either. But the passing attack for the Badgers has been inconsistent, and even after his breakout game against Notre Dame in Week 1, he hasn’t been the force we all hoped he’d be. Fortunately for the Badgers, they just got Jaylon Domingeaux back from injury last week and caught a pair of passes, so there is at least some more depth at receiver. home.headline: Iowa football's Kirk Ferentz on injuries, quarterbacks, Wisconsin
home.blurb: Iowa's top running back was injured in the first half of the game against Minnesota and did not return to the game. Ferentz announced that Moulton will miss the rest of the season. "We're not just pulling numbers out of the air," Ferentz said on the decision-making process for the starter. "We're trying to be as critical as we can and as fair as you can, too. If we do something, we usually have a reason for it, and it's hopefully well thought out and grounded in substance." "It just gets down to appreciating, understanding the value of the ball, and secondly, really keeping their concentration where it needs to be," Ferentz said. "And that's where the experience and inexperience can play in a little bit. I think we just got to do a better job at concentrating when it comes to that. I can't remember a game where it (the ball) was out as much as that." away.headline: Former USC TE could make season debut for Lobos against North Dakota State
away.blurb: New Mexico tight end Joey Olsen is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against North Dakota State, per an availability report released by the Mountain West on Thursday. The 6-foot-5, 246-pound junior transferred to UNM in January after playing sparingly over two seasons at Southern California. He tore his ACL during offseason workouts and has been listed as out on every availability report but Thursday's. Head coach Jason Eck first indicated that Olsen could potentially return this season in August, lauding the Lake Oswego, Oregon native's work ethic in rehabbing his injury. "Joey, he's going to keep stepping up … I do think he's probably looking (to return) more near the end of this month," Eck said on Oct. 5. "Maybe that Halloween game (against San Jose State) or something would be maybe his first thing, just getting enough months (removed) from his surgery that way." If Olsen is able to return, he would provide UNM with another receiving option in a tight end room that's been led by Cade Keith (15 catches for 212 yards, 2 touchdowns). Rated as a three-star prospect out of Lakeridge (Ore.) High School, Olsen caught 36 passes for 650 yards and 11 touchdowns as a senior to finish as the Pacers' all-time receptions (119) and yards (2,303) leader. Offensive lineman Cole Millward is also listed as questionable for Saturday's game. Eck said the 6-5, 297-pound senior tweaked his ankle early in UNM's 21-10 win over Hawaii.
